Lawmakers in Panama form Taiwan group
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:44 UTC
01:37:44 KST

The Panamanian National Assembly on Tuesday established a friendship group with the Legislative Yuan, a move welcomed by Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) as an opportunity to facilitate bilateral exchanges and advance mutual interests.
The multiparty interparliamentary exchange group was established at an inaugural ceremony at the assembly in Panama City.
Forty-five of the assembly’s 71 lawmakers have joined the group, including National Assembly President Shirley Castanedas and vice presidents Manuel Cohen and Manuel Cheng, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement released yesterday.
Photo: Huang Ching-hsuan, Taipei Times
In a congratulatory video message played during the inaugural ceremony, Lin said that Taiwan and Panama share universal values, including democracy, freedom and respect for human rights.
“Through the Taiwan-friendly parliamentary group, we look forward to further deepening parliamentary diplomacy and expanding bilateral cooperation and exchanges, thereby promoting the well-being of both peoples and fostering mutual benefit and shared prosperity,” the ministry quoted Lin as saying in the video.
The ministry said that the group was formed after more than 20 Panamanian lawmakers visited Taiwan over the past six months.
Taiwan and Panama ended formal diplomatic ties in June 2017.
In a separate video message played during the ceremony, US Representative Mario Diaz-Balart, cochair of the US Congressional Taiwan Caucus, congratulated the Panamanian National Assembly on establishing the parliamentary exchange platform, the ministry said.
Panamanian lawmaker Jose Antonio Perez-Barboni said the establishment of a Taiwan-Panama parliamentary exchange group was “a step in the right direction” and marked the beginning of closer economic and trade ties between the two sides.
He said he looked forward to advancing bilateral diplomatic relations.
Another lawmaker, Joan Manuel Guevara, said the formation of the parliamentary exchange group demonstrated that Taiwan and Panama could continue to develop “parliamentary diplomacy” despite the absence of formal diplomatic relations.
Such cooperation is particularly important as both sides seek to defend their sovereignty and withstand external pressure, Guevara said.
Perez-Barboni and Guevara are members of the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC).
Panamanian lawmakers have stepped up parliamentary exchanges with Taiwan over the past two years, with multiple delegations visiting Taiwan.
IPAC members led delegations to Taiwan in November last year and February, while Orlando Carrasquilla, chairman of the Panamanian National Assembly’s Committee on Agricultural and Fisheries Affairs, led a delegation to Taiwan in July.
When Perez-Barboni led a delegation to Taiwan in February, he was chairman of the National Assembly’s Committee on Infrastructure and Canal Affairs.
The itineraries of the delegations, their membership and the lawmakers’ public remarks indicate that Panama has been interested in Taiwan’s technological and economic development, suggesting that parliamentary exchanges between the two sides are increasingly focused on practical cooperation in technology and trade.

16:37:43 UTC
01:37:43 KST

Taipei prosecutors have questioned an aide who on Sunday allegedly met with Chang Chun-chieh (張俊傑), the office manager of indicted independent Legislator Kao Chin Su-mei (高金素梅), before Chang jumped bail.
The Taipei District Prosecutors’ Office said in a statement that it and the New Taipei City Police Department's Xindian Precinct on Tuesday searched the homes of Chang, his daughter, and another aide to Kao Chin, surnamed Chen (陳), who was also summoned for questioning.
Additional searches were yesterday conducted at Chen’s office at the Legislative Yuan, prosecutors said, adding that she was later granted bail of NT$50,000 (US$1,589) and placed under residency restrictions.
Photo: Liu Yung-yun, Taipei Times
Chen met with Chang at about 10am on Sunday and the two shared a meal for less than an hour, during which time Chang is suspected of giving Chen unspecified objects, local Chinese-language news reports said.
The alleged contact came hours before Chang’s electronic wrist monitor sent out a low-battery alert on Sunday night. Responding police discovered that Chang had gone missing and his monitor had been broken and discarded.
An arrest warrant was issued for Chang, but as of yesterday he had not been found.
Kao Chin, Chang and 22 others were on June 8 indicted on corruption and fraud-related charges related to the embezzlement of public funds and the importation of unapproved COVID-19 test kits from China.
Kao Chin, who has denied wrongdoing, is accused of fraudulently obtaining more than NT$7.87 million in public funds through fraudulent claims for legislative assistant salaries, bonuses, overtime pay and childcare subsidies.
Kao Chin registered several individuals, including her siblings, as legislative assistants, despite them not actually performing any duties, prosecutors said.
Chang is accused of conspiring with Kao Chin to fraudulently obtain funds earmarked for assistant salaries, as well as using an indigenous cultural association to fraudulently obtain more than NT$9.33 million from government agencies and state-owned enterprises.
During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2022, Kao Chin also authorized Chang to enlist others to illegally import 74,400 unapproved rapid test kits from China, circumventing medical device regulations, prosecutors said.
However, Kao Chin has said that the rapid test kits were intended to help indigenous communities amid a shortage of the devices in Taiwan.
In the indictment, prosecutors recommended a sentence of at least 16 years for Chang and 12.5 years for Kao Chin.
Chang, who was held incommunicado for nearly four months before he was charged, was released on NT$10 million bail in June.
At the time, Chang’s lawyers sought his release on health grounds as he is over the age of 70 and battling lung cancer.
During the first day of his trial on Sept. 1, Chang denied the corruption charges but admitted to other offenses, such as document forgery.
He said that he was not a legislative aide in name only, but had actually performed his duties and lacked criminal intent.

====================================================================================================

Exports hit record on 41% rise
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:43 UTC
01:37:43 KST

Exports hit a record last month as artificial intelligence (AI) demand continued to spread across semiconductors, servers and other high-tech products, the Ministry of Finance said yesterday.
Exports rose 41 percent from a year earlier to US$82.4 billion, the highest monthly level on record, the ministry said.
The gain marked the 34th consecutive month of year-on-year growth and exceeded the ministry’s expectations of growth of 31 to 35 percent on better-than-expected AI demand.
Photo: CNA
“We underestimated the strength of AI, which is spreading rapidly into more technology sectors,” Department of Statistics Director-General Beatrice Tsai (蔡美娜) said.
The momentum is likely to continue into the final months of the year, with the ministry expecting exports to grow by more than 40 percent this month as the peak season for high-tech products begins.
Monthly exports in the fourth quarter could average as high as US$83 billion, Tsai said, a level Taiwan has never reached.
The increasingly broad adoption of AI is helping to support global economic activity and cushion the effects of short-term disruptions such as tariff uncertainty, Tsai said.
Information, communications and audiovisual products, as well as electronic components remained the main engines of growth, with the categories together accounting for 78.7 percent of total exports last month, the ministry said.
The concentration highlights Taiwan’s pivotal role in the global AI supply chain, while also underscoring the economy’s increasing dependence on technology-related demand.
“AI has created a wave that keeps strengthening demand,” Tsai said, adding that Taiwanese companies occupy key positions in global semiconductor and server supply chains.
The upcoming launch of new mobile devices also provided an additional boost as international brands began building inventories, Tsai said.
However, supply constraints across parts of the electronics industry have yet to be fully resolved, supporting prices and increasing the value of shipments, she said.
The release of Apple Inc’s latest iPhone lineup, including an expected foldable model, is likely to provide support for Taiwan’s electronics suppliers as buyers and manufacturers prepare for the new devices, the ministry said.
Mineral products were another major contributor to Taiwan’s exports growth, with outbound shipments jumping about 70 percent last month as higher oil prices increased the value of petroleum-related goods, it said.
Last month, imports rose even faster, climbing 44.3 percent to US$60.1 billion, it said.
The increase reflected the increasingly international division of labor in AI supply chains, as Taiwanese manufacturers sourced more components and materials from overseas, including memory chips from South Korea, the ministry said.
Capital goods imports jumped 41.6 percent to US$13.06 billion, pointing to continued investment by local technology companies as they expand production capacity to meet customer demand, it said.
The export performance pushed the trade surplus to a record US$22.3 billion that month, up 32.9 percent from a year earlier, the ministry said.
For the first eight months of this year, exports jumped 44.2 percent to US$574.34 billion from the same period last year, while imports rose 40.4 percent to US$437.4 billion over the period, it said.
The ministry expects export momentum to remain strong through the end of the year, Tsai said.

Brace for new AI threats ahead of elections, AIT head says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:43 UTC
01:37:43 KST

Taiwan must guard against artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled information manipulation ahead of local elections on Nov. 28, American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Director Raymond Greene said yesterday.
Although Taiwan has earned acclaim for its efforts to counter disinformation, it must still brace for a new wave of sophisticated, AI-powered cognitive warfare, Greene said during his keynote speech at the Taipei Security Dialogue hosted by the Institute for National Defense and Security Research.
Taiwan also urgently needs to defend financial institutions and critical infrastructure against AI-powered cyberattacks, he said.
Photo: Tien Yu-hua, Taipei Times
The US’ top diplomat in Taiwan also touched on issues such as defense spending, military reforms and energy resilience.
Taiwan has made great progress in energy resilience by increasing the importation and storage of liquefied natural gas, which the international community has taken note of, Greene said.
The nation has also made less visible, but equally impressive, improvements in its electricity allocation policy, power-grid decentralization, use of coal-fired plants and renewables, and exploration of alternative energy sources, including small modular reactors and geothermal energy, he said.
Washington welcomes President William Lai’s (賴清德) commitment to increase defense spending to 5 percent of GDP by 2030, as US allies face rising security threats around the globe, he said.
US President Donald Trump has been calling on European countries to take on greater responsibilities for their self-defense, he said, adding that Ukraine has shown that sustained military spending can improve a nation’s military capabilities.
Compared with many other US partners, Taiwan is far better placed financially to boost its defense, Greene said.
Military preparedness should not just aim to win a war, but to prevent a conflict from breaking out altogether, he said.
Deterring Chinese aggression is paramount for Taiwan and the world, he said.
“Beyond the human toll, any conflict across the Taiwan Strait would have a bigger impact on the global economy than the Second World War,” Greene said.
The Trump administration has made preserving peace in the Indo-Pacific region one of its top priorities, he said.
That includes “vigorous” diplomacy, especially at the highest levels, he said.
“The upcoming US-China summit is an opportunity to further advance a relationship of strategic stability, on the basis of fairness and reciprocity, that can avoid misunderstandings and miscalculations,” Greene added.
At the same time, the US is reinforcing its presence and partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region to maintain a “favorable regional balance of power,” while supporting Taiwan’s work to enhance its ability to defend itself, he said.
Claims that Taiwan’s efforts to bolster national defense are provocative and accusations that the US aims to change the “status quo” in the region are false, he said.
Taiwan has been rapidly implementing lessons learned from Ukraine’s use of asymmetric warfare and emerging technology to fend off Russia’s invasion, Greene said.
Taiwan has many strategic advantages Ukraine and many other countries do not have, including advanced manufacturing capabilities, sea barriers and formidable natural geography, he said.
Taiwan’s armed forces are rapidly adapting to mission-command concepts, as demonstrated in the latest Han Kuang exercises, he added.
Such flexibility has been vital in Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s military, which has been hobbled by its rigid and hierarchical command structure, Greene said.
Taiwan and the US must constantly improve their defensive capabilities to safeguard peace, he said.

Edgar Grospiron, president of the organizing committee for the 2030 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games in the French Alps, is set to leave his post just 18 months after his appointment, a source with direct knowledge of the matter said yesterday.
Negotiations are under way over the terms of his departure, which is backed at “the highest levels of the French State,” the source said, capping a rocky period marked by governance disputes and a string of senior departures.
The move is expected to be formalized at an executive board meeting today.
Photo: AFP
The source, who declined to be named because they were not authorized to discuss the matter, said Grospiron had come close to being ousted during the Milan-Cortina Winter Games earlier this year.
On that occasion, director general Cyril Linette left instead, citing “insurmountable disagreements” with Grospiron.
Key Games stakeholders, including the French government, the Provence-Alpes-Cote d’Azur and Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes regions, and the French Olympic and Paralympic committees told the International Olympic Committee late last month that “trust had been broken” with Grospiron, the source said.
The rupture followed a tense executive board meeting on July 23 at which Grospiron sought to push through two appointments, the source added.
Two days later, French Olympic Committee president Amelie Oudea-Castera told local media that the project was “once again facing governance problems.”
Grospiron, the 1992 Olympic moguls champion, was appointed in February last year and had already faced a governance crisis earlier this year.
That culminated in Linette’s departure in February following a series of other senior exits, including those of the organizing committee’s operations director and communications director.

Asian Games athletes and venues unharmed by floods
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:37 UTC
01:37:37 KST

Athletes who had arrived early for the Asian Games were unharmed by extensive flooding that hit the central Japanese city of Nagoya, Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa said yesterday.
“We are not worried about the conditions of the venues and we believe there is no problem holding the Asian Games as planned,” Hirosawa said.
The Asian Games, an event with more athletes than the Summer Olympics, open on Saturday next week in Nagoya and surrounding areas and run through Oct. 4.
Photo: AP
More than 11,000 athletes are signed up from 45 countries and regions in Asia. By comparison, about 10,700 athletes participated in the Summer Olympics in 2024 in Paris.
The previous edition of the Asian Games was held three years ago in Hangzhou, China.
Hirosawa said about 400 athletes and staff who are staying in converted shipping containers — remodeled to serve as temporary housing units for the Asian Games — were briefly evacuated to higher ground during the heavy rain.
He said there were a number of leaking roofs, but nothing more serious around the dozens of Games venues.

Taipei to launch more food-safety inspections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:37 UTC
01:37:37 KST

The Taipei City Government is to conduct more unannounced inspections to ensure food safety at schools, Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) said yesterday, following an alleged food poisoning incident at a high school on Monday, in which 87 students became ill.
The school was ordered to suspend lunch services on Tuesday.
Taipei on Monday last week launched a free school lunch program for all elementary and junior-high school students.
Photo: Chang Chia-ming, Taipei Times
On Tuesday, Democratic Progressive Party Taipei City Councilor Lin Liang-chun (林亮君) said she received complaints from parents saying that the lunch provided at a school on Monday contained suspected spoiled meat and some students complained about the smell.
Lin said she has asked the Taipei Department of Health to clarify the situation.
Taipei Department of Health Food and Drug Division Director Lin Kuan-chen (林冠蓁) on Tuesday said the department received a report from the school at about noon on that day saying that 87 students experienced diarrhea and displayed suspected food poisoning symptoms from 10pm on Monday.
The department sent inspectors to the school to investigate and collect samples for examination, and it also ordered the lunch service to be suspended, Lin Kuan-chen said.
On-site inspection found five hygiene deficiencies, and the department ordered the school to implement improvements before tomorrow, or face fines of up to NT$200 million (US$6.35 million), she said.
The health department said it also collected 11 food, environment and hand swab samples from the kitchen for testing.
All the affected children have returned to school, and the city government would set up a special project to follow up on the case and the children’s health, Chiang said yesterday.
The ingredients are being traced to the source and environmental sanitization has been conducted, he said, adding that the city government would increase unannounced campus food safety inspections.
The health department yesterday evening said that education department officials also went to the school to investigate the case, and the preliminary inspection showed that the meat in Monday’s lunch met Certified Agricultural Standards requirements for traceability.
People should pay close attention to the hygienic conditions of food-handling and eating venues, avoid raw or undercooked food, and eat meals promptly to prevent food poisoning, the health department said.
Those who experience suspected food poisoning symptoms should seek medical attention immediately and report the incident, it said.

Wong’s benchmark salary would jump to S$3.6 million from S$2.2 million.

Peanut butter art ends run
An artwork consisting of 390kg of peanut butter spread on the floor of a Dutch museum attracted 48,000 visitors, 48 accidental footprints, five phones and one “licking incident” during its run, the institution said on Tuesday. The unusual work, a tribute to artist Wim T. Schippers who died this year, was on display for two months at the Boijmans van Beuningen museum in Rotterdam. Peanut butter was spread on a hexagonal floor measuring 25m2 “as smoothly as possible, without any lumps,” according to the artist’s instructions. “Forty-eight visitors made a fatal misstep into the floor,” the museum said in a statement summing up the exhibition. “Five phones were fished out.” It added that there was one licking incident, with a spokesperson saying that a young child was thought to be the culprit.

Imported mpox cases rise from last year: CDC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:35 UTC
01:37:35 KST

The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) yesterday reported two new cases of mpox, including a locally acquired case infected with the newer Mpox Clade Ib strain.
It added that mpox cases this year had reached 30, double the number for the same period last year.
The two new confirmed cases include a local case and an imported case, the centers said.
Photo: Lin Chih-yi, Taipei Times
Both cases reported having unsafe sex before the onset of symptoms and were unvaccinated against mpox, it said.
The local case is a man in his 40s who began having symptoms last month, including mouth sores, a fever and rash. The imported case is a man in his 30s, who traveled to Cambodia last month and engaged in unsafe sexual activity, and later experienced fever, chills and rash, it said.
CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Ming-cheng (林明誠) said that as of Monday, 30 cases of mpox have been reported this year — 20 locally acquired and 10 imported — all men aged between 20 and 60.
While the number of local cases has been declining, the percentage of imported cases has increased, he said, adding that the 10 imported cases reported this year were double the figure for the same period last year.
The risk of contracting mpox overseas cannot be overlooked, he said.
Of the 10 imported cases this year, six were from Thailand, and one each from Vietnam, India, Hong Kong and Cambodia, the CDC said.
Epidemiological data from other countries show that both Clade II and the newer Clade Ib virus strains of mpox might cause symptoms including fever, swollen lymph nodes and rash or blisters, but systemic rashes are more widely distributed over the body in Clade Ib, Lin said.
Clade Ib can spread more readily through household contacts compared with Clade II, and immunocompromised people, young children, pregnant women, or those with chronic illnesses are more likely to experience severe illness, he said.
The overall symptoms and fatality rates of Clade Ib and Clade II are similar, and the severity of mpox infection depends heavily on the status of a person’s immune system, the CDC said.
Mpox vaccines can provide effective protection against Clade Ib infection, and the antiviral drug Tecovirimat can help treat a severe Clade Ib infection, it added.
Getting the first dose of the standard two-dose mpox vaccine regimen only provides about 40 to 80 percent protection, while completing the full two-dose series can increase effectiveness up to 90 percent, Lin said.
Since the mpox vaccine was introduced in Taiwan, 111,908 people have received the first dose, while 80,033 people completed two doses, he said, adding that the CDC strongly urges the roughly 29 percent who did not get their second dose to get fully vaccinated as soon as possible.

Mao’s shadow hangs over China 50 years on
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:37:34 UTC
01:37:34 KST

China yesterday marked half a century since the death of Mao Zedong (毛澤東), founder of the People’s Republic, who brought roughly one-quarter of the world’s population under communist rule and whose specter still haunts China’s future.
Mao’s death on Sept. 9, 1976, at age 82, mourned by many and welcomed by some who suffered under his nearly three-decade rule, also hastened the end of the Cultural Revolution, a frenzied mass movement he launched in 1966.
The party later condemned the Cultural Revolution as a grave error for which Mao bore primary responsibility, but still reveres him, saying his achievements outweigh his mistakes.
Photo: EPA
Mao’s 6m-high portrait overlooks Beijing’s Tiananmen Square, the symbolic center of Chinese political power. His preserved body lies in the Chairman Mao Memorial Hall, where visitors from across the country queue to pay respects.
Many still idolize Mao as the nation’s savior. The mausoleum extended hours for the anniversary, expecting a surge in visitors.
During the Cultural Revolution, a distrustful and aging Mao mobilized students and supporters against perceived “class enemies,” including leaders accused of “taking the capitalist road,” unleashing upheaval that fractured the bureaucracy, paralyzed the economy and triggered violence and persecution.
The decade of turmoil also left a complex imprint on generations of leaders who followed Mao, including Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平).
Xi’s father, former Chinese vice premier Xi Zhongxun (習仲勛), was purged and brutally persecuted in the lead-up to and during the Cultural Revolution, while the family home was ransacked.
The teenage Xi Jinping was labeled a “reactionary student,” subjected to interrogation and coercive political study and even threatened with execution.
“Because I had a stubborn streak and refused to be bullied, I offended the rebel faction,” Xi Jinping said in a 2000 interview with a state-run magazine. “Everything bad was blamed on me... I wasn’t even 15.”
In 1969, like many others of his generation, Xi Jinping was sent to the countryside and spent seven years in a poverty-stricken village in northwestern China.
“The Cultural Revolution was a profoundly disillusioning experience for Xi,” said Joseph Torigian, an expert in Chinese politics at American University.
However, “he still saw something redemptive in the campaign,” which toughened him and showed the dangers of state collapse and that the party needed a clear road map to socialism, Torigian added.
Xi Jinping has not publicly blamed Mao for either his family’s suffering or other tragedies he witnessed.
Since becoming China’s top leader in 2012, he has instead argued that the post-Mao reform era should not be used to repudiate the Maoist years, while increasingly echoing Mao-era practices.
Unlike his immediate predecessors who — prompted by Deng Xiaoping’s (鄧小平) reforms in the aftermath of Mao — sought to cautiously loosen the leader’s grip, Xi Jinping has unapologetically consolidated power, cultivated personal authority and stressed ideological conformity and strict party discipline.
He is on course to become the longest-serving paramount leader of the People’s Republic of China, after Mao, having broken with reform-era term limit norms meant to curb excessively concentrated power and reduce the risk of another personality cult.
Xi Jinping has also had his own name formally attached to the state ideology enshrined in both the party and state constitutions, a feat no other since Mao has managed while in office.
“The iconography of Maoism, the charisma, and very specific language and symbols — these remain immensely powerful,” said Kerry Brown, director of King’s College London’s Lau China Institute.
“Xi has reinstated some of this with strong nationalism and populism,” he added.
One reason Xi Jinping shies away from more direct criticism of Mao is that he “wants to take the party back to its glory days when everyone was shaped by zeal and enthusiasm,” Torigian said.
The question is whether Xi Jinping’s approach will prove lasting, “or whether, like Mao before him, Xi is unintentionally creating pressure for change that will push China in a new direction after he’s gone,” he added.

CIA director may take leading role in US talks on Russia-Ukraine war – FT
CIA Director John Ratcliffe may take a leading role in Washington's diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.
Source: Financial Times citing informed sources, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The White House is reportedly considering reducing the involvement of US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, who have so far played a key role in contacts with Moscow and Kyiv.
Officials close to Ratcliffe told European counterparts that he will play a larger role in "shuttle diplomacy" between Russia and Ukraine.
Ratcliffe is expected to continue maintaining contacts with the intelligence services of both countries. However, the sources said Trump has not yet made a final decision.
The sources said Witkoff, for his part, is likely to retain his position as US special envoy for peace missions, which includes negotiations in the Middle East. They said he may continue to take part in the Ukraine process in parallel with Ratcliffe.
Two of the sources said Ratcliffe and Witkoff are engaged in a struggle over who will be responsible for what.
Background:
- On 25 August, it was reported that the CIA director visited Moscow. Speaking about Ratcliffe's trip, US President Donald Trump has said "something may come out of it".
- On 6 September, after talks in Kyiv involving the Ukrainian side, Trump's special envoys and national security advisers from the E3 countries, an agreement was reached to repeat the meeting in the same format in the near future.

Watch: Norway bids farewell to King Harald
Tributes have been paid to King Harald V after his funeral in Norway's capital Oslo, with the Prince of Wales and other European royals among attendees.
Flags were raised from half-mast to mark the conclusion of a private ceremony at Akershus Fortress, where the king was laid to rest in the crypt of the Palace Chapel after a public service at Oslo Cathedral.
Tens of thousands of people lined the streets to pay their respects after 13 days of national mourning.
The new king Haakon VIII - Harald's son - and his family stood on the balcony of the Royal Palace and waved to thousands of people gathered outside.
The late monarch died in August after 35 years on the throne.

On 7 September, MFA Secretary of State Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski met with Grata Endah Werdaningtyas, Director General of American and European Affairs at Indonesia's Ministry for Foreign Affairs. The talks focused on fostering bilateral relations, security in Europe, and the situation in the Indo-Pacific region.
The interlocutors emphasised the importance of regular political dialogue for the furthering strengthening of Polish–Indonesian relations. They discussed opportunities to intensify economic cooperation, particularly in the agri-food, energy, new technologies, and green technology sectors. They also noted the need to continue supporting cooperation between businesses from Poland and Indonesia.
Deputy Foreign Minister Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski highlighted the significance of Poland’s accession to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) in July 2026. The accession reflects Poland’s growing engagement in the Indo-Pacific region and creates additional opportunities for developing cooperation with the member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). Poland regards Indonesia as an important partner in the region and is interested in a further deepening of relations, both bilaterally and within the framework of EU–ASEAN cooperation. The Indonesian side pointed to the success of Poland’s economic transformation and emphasised its interest in Poland’s experience, which serves as an important reference point for cooperation between the two countries, including within the G20 framework.
An exchange of views on international affairs and security was an important element of the talks. Among other topics, Deputy Minister Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski and Director General Grata Endah Werdaningtyas discussed the situation in Europe and the Indo-Pacific, Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, and the key challenges to the international order. They stressed the importance of respect for international law, the principles of the Charter of the United Nations, and effective multilateralism.
The talks confirmed the broad potential for strengthening relations between Poland and Indonesia, both bilaterally and in the context of cooperation with ASEAN.
***
ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) was established in Bangkok in 1967. It is a political and economic organisation based in Jakarta.

Meta launches personal AI agent Muse that can shop, book travel, negotiate for users
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:35:32 UTC
01:35:32 KST

Halis Sünnetci
09 September 2026•Update: 09 September 2026
Meta launched a new personal artificial intelligence agent on Tuesday called Muse, designed to carry out tasks on users' behalf rather than simply respond to questions.
The US technology company said Muse can make purchases, book travel, send emails, fill out forms and negotiate on behalf of users.
Once given a task or broader goal, Muse can develop a personalized plan and continue working independently, including after users close the app.
The agent can return when circumstances change or when it needs approval, with Meta saying it seeks permission before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase.
Muse can complete online purchases using Stripe's Link payment service, which can generate a single-use virtual card for an approved purchase while keeping users' underlying payment details hidden from the agent.
Muse can also remember information users previously shared and use it to make suggestions without being prompted.
The agent operates through what Meta calls a Secure VM, a dedicated virtual computer in the cloud with its own browser that allows it to interact with websites and connected services.
A separate AI agent called Sentinel governs Muse's access to the internet and connected services, determining whether an action can proceed, should be blocked or requires the user's approval.
Users can choose which services Muse can access and what it is allowed to do within them, while Meta said the agent cannot see users' passwords or payment methods, and provides an audit trail of its actions.
The company said conversations and data stored in Muse's virtual machine are not shared with its advertising systems, while users can opt out of having their interactions used to train Meta's AI models.
The launch comes as AI companies face questions about the security and privacy risks of giving autonomous agents access to users' personal accounts and data.
Muse is initially available to those aged 18 and older in the US through a dedicated app or WhatsApp, with support for Meta's AI glasses planned.
The service is free for most uses, while subscription plans for heavier use are priced at $20 and $100 per month.

European Parliament to debate Ceuta crisis amid fierce political backlash
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:33:44 UTC
01:33:44 KST

The EPP and other right-wing groups are pushing for a resolution that would criticise Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and call for a tougher migration policy, while the Socialists and Democrats are expected to defend Spain and call for greater European solidarity.
The European Parliament will debate the situation in Ceuta next Tuesday in Strasbourg, in what is expected to be a heated political confrontation, following a decision by the Parliament’s political group leaders in Brussels on Wednesday.
The centre-right European People’s Party (EPP) and the European Conservatives and Reformists (ECR) also pushed to add a resolution to be voted on by lawmakers after the debate, in a move widely seen as an attempt to attack the Spanish government led by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
The debate is expected to be contentious, with the EPP poised to confront Sánchez directly.
“The Prime Minister said [the Ceuta crisis] has been an attack on Spain's territorial integrity. But he has not acted consequently”, EPP senior MEP Javier Zarzalejos said at a press conference on Tuesday.
Besides the EPP, otherright-wing conservative and far-right parties are also ready to attack Sánchez, linking the massive influx into Ceuta to the Spanish plan for the mass regularisation of undocumented migrants.
The Socialists and Democrats (S&D) group will be on the defensive, calling for European solidarity with Spain and criticising other governments for failing to present a united front following the sudden arrival of thousands of migrants in Ceuta.
“The narrative adopted by some prime ministers was simply shocking. They attacked Spain instead of showing support,” a senior S&D MEP told Euronews on condition of anonymity.
The final title of the debate reflects a compromise between differing political positions. The Parliament’s agenda lists it as: “The recent hybrid attacks and instrumentalisation of migrants in Ceuta and the need for a coordinated response to protect the EU’s external borders.”
The resolution, expected to be put to a vote next Tuesday, is likely to trigger a dispute over amendments shaping its final wording, with right-wing groups expected to press for a tougher stance on migration and criticism of Spain’s handling of the crisis.
The Spanish exclave is “on the brink of collapse”, according to its president, after the massive arrival of some 80,000 irregular migrants on 30 July. Several thousand of them, including unaccompanied minors, are still in the city, sparking a humanitarian crisis and making the overall situation “untenable”, Ceuta’s president said.
Meanwhile, Madrid has been plunged into further chaos after a leaked police report suggested that Moroccan forces played a role in pushing migrants into Ceuta, a claim Sánchez has so far not confirmed.
The crisis also had consequences at the European level, with twenty-two EU countries calling for an emergency meeting in August and Italy reintroducing border checks at its air and maritime borders with Spain.
On Wednesday, the European Commission decided to provide Spain with €114.7 million in emergency assistance to help manage the situation, following a request submitted by Madrid on 24 August.

Comment Macron est devenu le meilleur allié de Mistral
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:33:16 UTC
01:33:16 KST

Nous sommes le 11 juin 2025. Alors que s’ouvre VivaTech, le patron de Mistral AI, Arthur Mensch, monte sur scène pour l’une des tables rondes les plus attendues du salon : l’à peine trentenaire, impeccablement cravaté, doit prendre la parole au côté de Jensen Huang, tout puissant PDG du géant des puces Nvidia, pour annoncer un partenariat stratégique entre les deux entreprises. Alors que le président Emmanuel Macron les rejoint avec quelques minutes de retard, l’Américano-Taïwanais se tourne vers le jeune patron français et lui glisse, d’un air entendu : “Your president worked really hard for you” [“Votre président s’est vraiment démené pour vous”].
Même pour le patron de la société la mieux valorisée au monde, ce volontarisme présidentiel surprend. Sur scène, le voilà qui fait rosir de plaisir le chef de l’Etat français, en illustrant son activisme : “J’ai dit au président qu’Arthur et Mistral avaient besoin du soutien des plus grandes entreprises françaises. Monsieur le président m’a dit : ‘Quelles sont-elles ? Laisse-moi les appeler !’”
Ce sera fait. Au moment d’officialiser leur accord, les deux entreprises et l’Elysée peuvent déjà annoncer que BNP Paribas, Orange, la SNCF ou encore Thales ont manifesté leur intérêt pour ce partenariat, qui a acté l’entrée de Mistral dans le domaine de la capacité de calcul informatique, maillon crucial de la chaîne de valeur de l’IA.
Advertisement
L’épisode relaté par le patron de Nvidia illustre tout à la fois l’inclinaison du gouvernement à promouvoir sa start-up nationale, et la manière dont Mistral a pris appui sur l’exécutif pour se hisser auprès des plus grandes entreprises d’IA générative.
Lancée en 2023 par trois cofondateurs, Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample et Timothée Lacroix, Mistral AI a d’emblée fait un choix : miser sur un lien étroit avec l’exécutif français, et en particulier avec Emmanuel Macron. Interrogés par POLITICO, une douzaine de responsables publics et de représentants de l’écosystème technologique décrivent ainsi la construction d’une relation privilégiée, qui a permis à Mistral de se faire une place auprès de l’Etat et à la table des leaders internationaux de l’IA.
Or, à quelques mois de l’élection présidentielle et alors que l’Europe s’interroge sur sa capacité à défier les champions technologiques chinois et américains et à gagner en indépendance technologique, Mistral AI est face à un tournant. L’entreprise, qui compte désormais plus de 1000 salariés, doit maintenant se projeter dans l’après-Macron.
Bonnes fées et millions
Dès sa naissance et sa première levée de fonds en 2023, la start-up — qui n’a pas souhaité répondre à POLITICO dans le cadre de cet article — a fait le choix de se rapprocher du secteur public. Ainsi, Bpifrance, la banque publique d’investissement française, fait partie de ses premiers investisseurs. “Nous avions conscience des enjeux de souveraineté liés à l’IA, et avions une bonne idée des rares — quelques centaines dans le monde alors — experts crédibles dans le secteur, dont les fondateurs de Mistral faisaient partie”, se souvient Arnaud Caudoux, le directeur général adjoint de Bpifrance. “C’était un montant record pour un tour d’amorçage français, mais il y avait beaucoup de bonnes fées autour du berceau”.
Les bonnes fées en question sont le gratin du capitalisme et du secteur technologique français, qui ont joué des rôles essentiels d’entremetteurs, de mécènes et de leveurs de fonds. Parmi eux, le milliardaire Xavier Niel, mais aussi Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve et Charles Gorintin, cofondateurs de la start-up spécialisée dans l’assurance Alan. En 2022, ils sont mus par un même objectif : contribuer à faire émerger un géant européen de l’intelligence artificielle. Ils ont ainsi activé leurs réseaux pour identifier les chercheurs français les plus prometteurs du secteur de l’IA.
Ce sont eux qui joueront les entremetteurs pour former le trio Arthur Mensch, Timothée Lacroix et Guillaume Lample. Au moment de “toper” avec les trois jeunes cofondateurs, l’équipe d’Alan obtient un ralliement stratégique pour tisser des liens avec le secteur public : Cédric O. L’ancien secrétaire d’Etat au Numérique, soutien d’Emmanuel Macron de la première heure, jouera un rôle majeur au moment du lancement de la start-up. C’est même lui qui montera au front à Bruxelles pour tenter d’obtenir des assouplissements sur le règlement européen sur l’IA (AI Act), présenté par la Commission européenne dès avril 2021.
Car, pour Mistral AI, ce texte est dangereux : comment bâtir un géant européen si l’Europe bride l’innovation ? Dès 2023, Cédric O se retrousse les manches et s’inscrit, au nom de Mistral, au registre de transparence de l’Union européenne afin de peser sur les négociations — au point même d’être soupçonné de conflit d’intérêts par certains parlementaires.
Advertisement
Ce nouveau venu s’attire rapidement les remontrances de Thierry Breton, alors commissaire européen : la start-up Mistral AI “fait du lobbying, c’est normal. Mais nous ne sommes dupes de rien. Elle défend son business aujourd’hui, et non, l’intérêt général”, critique Breton lors les dernières semaines de négociations autour de l’AI Act.
“Le rôle de Cédric O a en quelque sorte été celui d’un paratonnerre”, reconnaît un responsable du secteur privé qui a suivi les débuts de Mistral. En prenant les coups, O a permis à Mensch “de grandir et de se construire en tant que PDG”, poursuit-il.
Dans les coulisses
Dès ses débuts, Mistral joue la carte française et européenne. Les trois cofondateurs ont beau avoir fait carrière dans les laboratoires d’intelligence artificielle américains (Google Deepmind pour Mensch, Facebook AI pour Guillaume Lample et Timothée Lacroix), les premières notes de concept, élaborées pour le lancement de la start-up, placent l’enjeu de la souveraineté technologique au cœur du projet.
A l’époque, Mensch est un discret ingénieur de trente ans qui doit entamer sa mue pour porter le discours de Mistral AI sur la scène internationale. En juin 2023, quelques mois après le lancement de sa start-up, l’ancien élève de Polytechnique fait sa première apparition publique aux côtés d’Emmanuel Macron sur la grande scène du salon technologique VivaTech, et commence à développer son discours sur l’autonomie technologique européenne. De quoi séduire le président français, qui en a fait l’une de ses martingales. “Comment la France et l’Europe envisagent de permettre l’émergence de champions européens et comment faire en sorte que la régulation de l’IA ne vienne pas gêner l’innovation ?” interroge alors le jeune entrepreneur, en chemise et baskets, face au président français.
Mensch sera chargé de contribuer lui-même aux réponses. Quelques mois plus tard, Matignon décide de former un comité d’experts pour établir une stratégie française pour l’IA. Outre Mensch et Cédric O, il sera composé de Gaël Varoquaux, chercheur à l’Inria et ancien directeur de thèse de Mensch, mais aussi du futur prix Nobel d’économie Philippe Aghion, et du chercheur chez Meta Yann LeCun.
En 2024, alors que le comité rend son rapport et que Mistral AI présente “Le Chat”, le concurrent du modèle d’Open AI ChatGPT, le paysage de l’IA est déjà en pleine mutation. Et l’Europe doute : le concurrent allemand Aleph Alpha, l’autre espoir européen de l’IA générative, annonce se détourner du développement de modèles propres. Avec un constat pessimiste : “le simple fait de disposer d’un LLM européen ne suffit pas comme modèle économique. Cela ne justifie pas l’investissement”, explique son patron, Jonas Andrulis. L’annonce plombe les espoirs européens de développer des modèles souverains.
Les doutes n’épargnent pas Mistral, et les observateurs sont nombreux à redouter un décrochage technologique par rapport à ses concurrents américains ou chinois — au point de craindre que la start-up soit rachetée par un géant de la tech. En 2025, des rumeurs d’échanges avec Apple, éventées par la presse, créent un vent de panique au sommet de l’Etat. L’ambassade française aux Etats-Unis et l’Elysée s’enquièrent auprès de Mistral de la réalité de ces échanges, selon deux conseillers sollicités par POLITICO. Ils sont finalement rassurés par l’entreprise : il n’y a pas eu d’échanges “au plus haut niveau”.
Partenaire stratégique
Pour l’exécutif, l’enjeu n’est plus seulement de promouvoir une jeune pousse prometteuse. L’Etat est désormais prêt à pousser les murs pour préserver une entreprise dont les technologies sont progressivement intégrées à tous les niveaux de l’Etat. Après avoir signé un partenariat stratégique avec France Travail début 2025, Mistral AI a en effet décroché un accord-cadre avec le ministère des Armées pour le développement de l’IA dans la défense.
Advertisement
Depuis 2025, “Le Chat” est aussi en cours de déploiement auprès de 10 000 agents publics. Pour adouber Mistral AI, le ministère de l’Action publique a dû se contorsionner. D’une part, car la direction interministérielle du numérique (Dinum) “voyait d’un très mauvais œil de recourir à une solution venue du privé”, indique un responsable ministériel qui a répondu anonymement pour évoquer des négociations internes à l’Etat. D’autre part, parce que la commande publique est soumise à des règles strictes d’ouverture à la concurrence, qui ne sont pas censées permettre de favoriser un acteur plutôt qu’un autre, même si celui-ci est français.
“Nous avons perdu quelques semaines car il fallait border juridiquement le process”, précise le responsable cité plus haut. “L’expérimentation d’outils est généralement une manière de permettre aux entreprises de mettre un pied dans la porte”, glisse un ancien conseiller gouvernemental.
A la table des grands
Si Mensch a tendance à minimiser l’importance des subventions publiques et du soutien des autorités à son entreprise, les équipes de Mistral reconnaissent volontiers que cette relation privilégiée est un atout majeur.
Avec l’aide de l’exécutif, l’entreprise française a pu décrocher plusieurs partenariats clés, dont un accord avec le géant néerlandais des semi-conducteurs ASML, en 2025. Bruno Le Maire, ministre de l’Economie durant sept ans avant de devenir conseiller stratégique d’ASML, a d’ailleurs été l’une des chevilles ouvrières de ce rapprochement. A la fin de la même année, Emmanuel Macron était à Berlin pour officialiser un accord avec un autre acteur européen du numérique : l’entreprise allemande spécialiste du logiciel SAP.
Cette proximité avec l’Elysée permet aussi à Mistral de pousser les portes des plus grands sommets internationaux. Elle a même eu une place de choix au sommet français sur l’IA, organisé à Paris début 2025. Pour l’occasion, l’Elysée a réservé le Grand Palais, ce dôme de verre bâti au cœur de la capitale pour l’Exposition universelle de 1900. Un lieu exceptionnel sur lequel Mistral AI a un temps envisagé de placer un logo géant — un “M” rouge et jaune pixellisé. Une idée finalement écartée “pour des raisons de sécurité”, s’amuse un ancien responsable public au fait des préparatifs.
Peu à peu, Mensch a donc pris ses habitudes dans les protocoles élyséens. Il est désormais de tous les déplacements présidentiels à l’étranger — ou presque. En décembre 2025, l’Elysée met presque par automatisme son nom dans la liste des chefs d’entreprises de la délégation d’Emmanuel Macron pour Pékin. Erreur : Mensch ne va pas en Chine. Un tel déplacement chez l’adversaire commercial des Etats-Unis pourrait mettre Mistral AI en délicatesse vis-à-vis des Américains, où l’entreprise compte un grand nombre d’investisseurs et de partenaires.
Ces déplacements officiels sont autant d’occasions, pour Mensch, d’affuter et d’internationaliser le contre-discours qu’il oppose à la Silicon Valley sur l’IA. Depuis plusieurs mois, le patron de Mistral AI, qui s’approprie volontiers la devise de Polytechnique (“Pour la Patrie, les Sciences et la Gloire”), martèle une position alignée sur celle d’Emmanuel Macron : il faut promouvoir l’autonomie technologique en Europe, et proposer au reste du monde un modèle plus sensible aux subtilités culturelles et linguistiques.
Advertisement
En février 2026, sur la scène du sommet de New Delhi où se sont pressés Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Demis Hassabis (Google Deepmind) et Sam Altman (OpenAI), Mensch poursuit sa croisade, défendant l’IA comme “un outil d’autonomisation, et non de domination”. “Je souhaite aborder un sujet un peu plus fondamental, à savoir : qui contrôle le déploiement de l’IA, qui en tire profit et comment pouvons-nous nous assurer qu’elle serve l’intérêt du plus grand nombre et non celui d’une minorité ?”, interroge-t-il.
Rebelote en juin, à Evian-les-Bains : lors d’un déjeuner avec les leaders du G7, Mensch endosse à nouveau le rôle du franc-tireur face à ses concurrents américains, qui appelaient à la rédaction de standards technologiques sous l’égide des Etats-Unis.“Les acteurs américains ont tendance à porter ce discours-là : faites-nous confiance, on va établir des standards chez nous et on vous les exportera”, mettait-il en garde auprès de POLITICO à l’issue de cette rencontre réunissant Donald Trump, Ursula von der Leyen ou encore Sam Altman.
Un consensus politique ?
Si Mistral compte indéniablement sur la scène internationale, reste à savoir ce que l’entreprise peut promettre : alors qu’elle a mis un pied dans les infrastructures en construisant des datacenters, et qu’elle poursuit le déploiement de ses solutions dans les grandes entreprises, certains commencent à douter que l’entreprise puisse rester dans la course pour produire des modèles “de frontière”, c’est-à-dire les plus performants.
Pour Emmanuel Macron, le dernier G7 a en tout cas été l’une des dernières opportunités d’imprimer sa marque dans le débat mondial sur l’IA. Et de permettre à Mistral de préparer l’après. Car la relation avec le futur locataire de l’Elysée reste à construire.
A ce stade, aucun candidat à l’élection présidentielle n’a remis en question le soutien public à la start-up. Certains se montrent toutefois plus allants, à l’instar de Gabriel Attal, qui met volontiers en scène sa proximité avec Mistral. Le candidat Renaissance a ainsi placé l’intelligence artificielle au cœur de son programme de campagne, et même intégré Le Chat dans sa boîte à outils de communication. Son concurrent Edouard Philippe (Horizons) fait de même, appuyé par ses lieutenants — la ministre de l’IA et du Numérique Anne Le Hénanff ou encore le député Laurent Marcangeli — qui assurent Mensch de leur soutien. Si Mistral ne s’affiche pas publiquement auprès du RN, le parti à la flamme voit lui aussi l’entreprise comme un atout souverain.
A gauche, personne n’a encore pris officiellement position, mais les partis ont unanimement soutenu l’entreprise — et appelé à une IA souveraine — face au risque de blocage de modèles américains illustré par Mythos, d’Anthropic, que Donald Trump a souhaité restreindre aux utilisateurs américains en juin dernier.
Advertisement
Mistral n’est toutefois pas pleinement souveraine : elle s’appuie, rappelons-le, sur des fonds internationaux et des partenariats d’ampleur avec les géants américains — Amazon, Nvidia ou encore Microsoft. “Il faut tuer cette idée, très café du commerce, qu’il serait faisable de détenir le capital, et donc financer seuls à l’échelle française ou européenne ces centaines de milliards qu’exigent les infrastructures IA. C’est juste impossible”, souligne le Secrétaire général pour l’investissement rattaché à Matignon, Bruno Bonnell.
Un détail qui pourrait mettre à mal l’unanimisme français en faveur de Mistral, alors que l’IA s’invite peu à peu dans les thèmes forts de la campagne.
Le front a d’ailleurs déjà commencé à se fissurer avec la proposition de loi de la sénatrice LR Laure Darcos, qui entend forcer les géants de l’IA à rémunérer le secteur culturel — un texte soutenu par la gauche et une partie de la droite, mais vivement rejeté par Mistral qui a finalement obtenu le soutien du bloc central et du gouvernement.
Autre caillou dans la chaussure de Mistral : un rapport parlementaire de juillet dernier, piloté par les députés Philippe Latombe (Modem) et Cyrille Chatelain (Ecologistes), estime que l’entreprise est devenue trop stratégique. Les deux élus proposent donc d’instaurer une “golden share” étatique au capital de la start-up pour éviter qu’elle ne soit vendue sans droit de regard de l’État.
Couvée dès sa naissance par le chef de l’Etat, Mistral voit donc la page de la macronie sur le point de se tourner, sans savoir exactement comment s’écrira la suivante. Ni sur quels alliés politiques elle pourra compter à partir de mai prochain.

Ukrainian UAVs attack Yamal in Russia for first time after flying almost 3,000 km – Russian media

Source: Meduza, a Russian independent news website; Dmitry Artyukhov, governor of Russia's Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug

Ukrainian Ai-Petri electronic warfare system capable of suppressing guided aerial bombs presented at exhibition in Poland – photos
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
19:31:00 EEST
01:31:00 KST

Ukrainian Ai-Petri electronic warfare system capable of suppressing guided aerial bombs presented at exhibition in Poland – photos
Ukraine's Ai-Petri electronic warfare system has been shown for the first time at the MSPO-2026 international exhibition in Poland. The system can jam drone control signals and suppress guided aerial bombs.
Source: a representative of Storkway, the company that developed and manufactures the system, in a comment to Ukrainska Pravda
Details: Development of the electronic warfare system began in 2014, when Russia annexed Crimea. The name Ai-Petri was chosen after the highest mountain in Crimea.
The Storkway representative said tactical-level systems have been supplied to the front since 2024 and were used, in particular, in cooperation with the 12th Special Purpose Centre. The company has already supplied around 400 electronic warfare systems, which operate along the entire contact line.
Quote: "It can be produced in two versions: fixed or mobile. It is transported on a pickup truck, can be easily deployed in 10 minutes by two crew members and begin operating. It consists of a rotating platform on which modules are installed, each with two channels, or jammers. The module also has a detection antenna and a radar that 'listens' to the radio frequencies of approaching drones."
More details: The electronic warfare system operates in the frequency range from 300MHz to 6GHz. Ai-Petri has a full-rotation function and scans the area across 360 degrees, while the coverage angle of one logarithmic antenna is about 45 degrees.
In detection mode, the system consumes 250W of power, rising to as much as 2,000W when jamming assets. The Storkway representative said that, depending on the terrain, the system can detect assets at a range of 20-30km.
Ai-Petri jams attack and reconnaissance drones and can also affect guided aerial bombs.
Quote: "Means of attack are evolving. We even have a slogan: if the enemy invents a virus, we immediately create an antivirus. Thanks to our military, they send feedback and we create new profiles to suppress new systems effectively and as quickly as possible."
More details: The manufacturer developed its own software for the Ai-Petri system, based on the Lyra situational awareness system. It allows data to be collected from other radars and creates a unified field for detecting and intercepting aerial threats.
Quote: "It can integrate with the radar field. The system has direct communication with Robin and Saab Giraffe radars, and our Lyra system brings all this information together and provides communication on what is located where, so that it can be guided effectively."
Background: It was reported earlier that Ukrainian company Unwave, which specialises in electronic warfare development, is upgrading its Bashur system for detecting and analysing UAV video signals. The system has been given a mesh network detection function, while its operating range has been expanded from 6GHz to 10GHz.

German defense minister defends record 2027 military budget
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:30:43 UTC
01:30:43 KST

Ayhan Şimşek
09 September 2026•Update: 09 September 2026
German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius on Wednesday defended a record 2027 military budget of about €140 billion ($163 billion), telling parliament the spending was a “security promise” amid growing uncertainty in the international arena and rising threats from Russia.
Speaking in the parliament’s budget debate, Pistorius dismissed opposition criticism that the increase should instead fund schools, hospitals and infrastructure upgrades. “They overlook the fact that a strong, capable German armed forces -- and a capable, united NATO -- are essential to protect our achievements and our way of life,” he said. “Without security, nothing else matters.”
Russia is rearming massively with money, personnel and materiel, Pistorius claimed, adding that Moscow spends half of its overall budget on military outlays, using large portions to replenish stockpiles for future conflicts rather than pouring those resources into the front lines in Ukraine.
“We are literally in Moscow’s crosshairs,” he told lawmakers. “Russia is attempting to spy on, influence, intimidate and destabilize our societies -- and, above all, to sow uncertainty among the people. And all of this has taken on a new dimension.”
Under the Merz government’s 2027 budget plan, defense is the second-largest federal budget item. The regular Defense Ministry chapter rises to €109.75 billion ($128 billion) in 2027, up 32.7% from this year -- the largest increase among major spending areas. Including money from the German military special fund, the ministry’s overall envelope next year approaches €140 billion ($163 billion).

Europe's royalty pay respects to King Harald V in Norway
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
17:30:28 BST
01:30:28 KST

Europe's royalty pay respects to King Harald V in Norway
- Published
Dozens of European royals and heads of state, including the Prince of Wales and three Nordic kings, have paid their last respects to King Harald V in Oslo.
Thousands of people lined the route during a funeral procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral on Wednesday afternoon, nearly two weeks after the king died aged 89.
After the ceremony and burial, the Norwegian royal family, including the new King Haakon, his wife Queen Mette-Marit, and his mother and Harald's widow Queen Sonja greeted crowds from the palace balcony.
A minute's silence was also observed throughout the country. Harald, who was seen as a popular, modernising figure, was on the Norwegian throne for 35 years.
After 13 days of national mourning, the day began on Wednesday with ceremonial troops assembling at Akershus Fortress, the medieval castle where Harald was later laid to rest.
A procession then took place, with Haakon, his sister Princess Märtha Louise and his children Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus, following the late king's coffin on foot.
Mette-Marit, who recently underwent a successful lung transplant, and Sonja, 89, followed in a car.
Prince William, representing his father King Charles III, attended the funeral alongside the Princess Royal, who was there in a personal capacity as godmother to Norway's new monarch.
They were among 30 royal figures from Sweden, Jordan, Monaco, Belgium, Spain, Japan and Denmark.
Among the non-royal heads of state attending the funeral were Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier along with five foreign prime ministers.
During the funeral service at the cathedral, Mette-Marit was seen wiping her eyes, as Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre delivered a eulogy, saying Harald had struck "a balance between being stately and down-to-earth and that he had "made Norway greater".
Queen Sonja, who was also visibly emotional during the ceremony, laid a red rose on Harald's coffin.
A poignant moment as three bell tolls marking the end of a minute's silence in the cathedral was briefly interrupted by a mobile phone alarm going off.
The day after his death, his son Haakon VIII thanked him for "being such a good dad" and said he had "always stayed true" to his values and commitments.
Royal observers have described the late king as well respected and beloved, and who was seen as a "grandfather" of the nation.
In the final months of his life, he and his family had faced personal challenges and scandal.
Earlier this year, documents revealed Mette-Marit's frequent contact with Jeffrey Epstein. She later said she wished she had never met the late sex offender.
Meanwhile, her son, Marius Borg Høiby - who is not a royal figure himself but grew up within the family - was given a four-year jail term for two counts of rape in June.
Høiby, who is under house arrest pending appeal, was granted permission to attend the funeral, and sat in the second row during the cathedral ceremony alongside Märtha Louise's children.
At the end of the service, four F-35 fighter jets flew over the cathedral in a "missing man" formation.
Harald's casket was then carried in a procession to the Palace Chapel at Akershus Fortress, where a private ceremony was attended by family members, foreign royals and other guests including the country's prime minister.
King Harald was laid to rest there alongside several members of the royal family, including his father King Olav V, his mother Crown Princess Märtha, and his grandparents, King Haakon VII and Queen Maud.
Norwegian flags across Oslo were raised from half mast to the top to mark the end of the burial, while the royal family returned to the royal palace.
In a display of gratitude for the support they had received since the king's death on 28 August, the family - Haakon, Mette-Marit, Ingrid Alexandra, Sverre Magnus and Sonja - then appeared on the balcony to greet tens of thousands of people who had gathered outside.

Temporary wartime weapons depot explosion kills 14 outside Syria's Idlib
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:30:25 UTC
01:30:25 KST

The blast at a temporary storage site for wartime munitions near the town of Sarmada left 11 others injured, with rescue teams still searching for survivors. A person is killed or wounded by unexploded ordnance every six hours in Syria today, according to humanitarian workers.
An explosion at a weapons depot near the northwestern city of Idlib killed at least 14 people and injured 11 others, Syria's Health Ministry said.
"The toll from the explosion in a temporary storage for collecting weapons and war remnants near the town of Sarmada ... registered 14 killed and 11 injured in a preliminary count," the Idlib health department said.
Security forces cordoned off roads leading to the Burj al-Nimra area on the road to Sarmada, some 45 kilometres from Idlib, as Civil Defence and Syrian Red Crescent first-responders continued to search for survivors trapped under the rubble.
Video footage widely circulated after the blast showed a large plume of black smoke and smaller explosions could be heard.
The depot was used to store weapons and munitions left over from the country's civil war from 2011 until 2024, according to authorities.
The cause of the blast near the town of Sarmada was not immediately clear. Initial assessments indicated the explosion was caused by munitions, said the head of emergency operations for Idlib's disaster management directorate, Walid Aslan.
Ahmad Faour, a mechanic who works near the warehouse, said he and others first heard a small explosion and ran away before the large blast.
"A weapons warehouse should not be placed in a public area, in a village with people and shops," he said, after looking through the damaged cars in his garage. "Those poor people who died were not guilty of anything."
The incident on Wednesday is the second deadly blast in Idlib this month, after a car carrying ammunition exploded, killing five in the city of Binnish.
A government source said at the time that the car was owned by a weapons trader, while authorities did not announce the cause of the blast.
Remnants of war
Syria is ranked among the world's most heavily contaminated countries for unexploded ordnance.
Explosions involving munitions-laden cars or arms depots have sporadically occurred in Idlib, a former front-line province where multiple armed factions stored weapons throughout the civil war which is among the most severely affected areas.
In November 2025, a blast at an ammunition depot in the Kafr Takharim area killed five workers and wounded nine.
In August 2025, an ammunition explosion on the outskirts of Idlib city killed four people and wounded five.
Humanitarian organisations called on Wednesday for intensified international and local efforts to clear mines and war remnants from the province, which they said continued to claim Syrian lives on a recurring basis.
UK mine-clearance charity HALO Trust estimated that this year unexploded ordnance was killing or wounding one person in Syria every six hours on average.
By August, some 700 casualties from explosive accidents were recorded, one-third of them deadly and one-third being children, according to Simon Jackson, HALO Trust's Syria programme manager.
According to Jackson, last year saw "a large spike in accidents as people rushed back to their communities" after the fall of al-Assad in December 2024.

You Can Now Destroy Flock Cameras for Cash in GTA V
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:30:00 UTC
01:30:00 KST

People are not happy about Flock Safety’s automated license plate readers and the cops that allegedly misuse them. If you’re one of those ALPR-haters, you can now take out your rage in the video game Grand Theft Auto V by installing Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader, a mod built by artist Morry Kolman.
The mod installs 235 Flock cameras around the fictional Los Santos, a riff on the real-life city of Los Angeles. Players can smash and shoot down the cameras and get paid $600 for each one they destroy, which Kolman priced based on a teardown of a Flock Falcon Flex Camera by the Iowa-based civil liberties group Eyes Off of Cedar Rapids. The in-game cameras log every time a player destroys and drives by one, and players can render a photo album of their interactions.
In real life, vigilantes have allegedly wrecked Flock cameras in their communities using spray-paint, saws, bullets, and even flaming projectiles. An NPR analysis found that Flock cameras have been vandalized in at least 36 states.
“GTPLR is not an endorsement of the activities that it allows in the game in the same way that GTA is not an endorsement of the activities that are allowed in the game,” says Kolman, referring to the fact that GTA is largely about doing fictional crimes. “But I think there is a public appetite for some kind of cathartic release against these machines.”
In addition to being fun objects to destroy, the GTA cameras also operate as an extension of the police in-game. Passing by one of the 235 cameras while being chased by the cops prolongs the game’s cooldown period. Because of how dense the cameras are in some areas, it can make the game impossible to play.
There’s also a 5 percent chance that the cameras will trigger a random police response even if the player isn’t doing anything wrong, which Kolman says was inspired by news reports about innocent people being held at gunpoint because of ALPR errors.
“There are violent responses and really dangerous situations that are created by these cameras and their inaccuracies,” says Kolman.
Flock did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this story.
GTA V has been around for over a decade, and a rich modding community has built up around it (WIRED covered one back in 2015.) The long-awaited sequel, Grand Theft Auto VI, is slated to come out in November and will be set in a fictional version of Miami called Vice City.
Kolman doesn’t have specific plans to build a version of GTALPR for that, joking, “We'll probably wait to see what the people of Vice City and their local government have already installed around their map.”
In real-life LA, the Los Angeles Police Department suspended its use of Flock cameras this summer following a recommendation from the LAPD’s inspector general. The tide is turning in other places too—governors in both Texas and Florida recently took steps to curtail the use of Flock cameras in their respective states, and across the US, there were 131 Flock contract terminations in August alone, according to the anti-surveillance advocacy group Secure Justice.
For all the fun that fake-smashing surveillance cameras can be, Kolman seriously hopes that players can feel the “insidiousness and inescapability of the surveillance” through GTALPR.
“I know that you could read a thousand articles about why surveillance is bad and why Flock is horrible,” says Kolman. “Or I could make you feel how pervasive these Flock cameras are by having you try to drive around the map of Los Santos.”

Defence minister Rajnath Singh meets Sri Lankan president Anura Kumara Dissanayake
Defence minister Rajnath conveyed greetings on behalf of PM Modi and underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical and civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges. He emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, “India considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as well”.Sri Lankan president Dissanayake said his country would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India’s security interests. He also expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Op Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New.
Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey bridges constructed by the Indian defence forces. The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between NCC and National Defence Colleges of both the countries.Rajnath also met Sri Lankan PM Harini Amarasuriya. “We exchanged views on a range of issues related to development cooperation, education and close cultural and civilisational ties,” he posted on X.
He underlined that as “sister democracies with shared heritage”, India and Sri Lanka should continue working towards a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region. Rajnath also highlighted Sri Lanka's importance in India's Vision MAHASAGAR, saying the island nation holds a special place in the policy and would continue to do so in the future.Rajnath called for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a favourable and secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests and brighter future. “Secure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region (IOR),” the defence minister said while addressing a gathering comprising Sri Lankan deputy minister of defence Aruna Jayasekara, commanders of the Sri Lankan three services.Rajnath said India and Sri Lanka are bound by the shared ocean, and maritime security is not a matter of abstract theory but a reality that shapes their trade, security and destinies. “Both nations are central to any strategic discourse on maritime security in the region. Strong India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation will be mutually beneficial and vital for collective growth and security,” he said.Referring to the challenges faced by our fishermen, the defence minister underscored that the issue needs to be addressed together. He observed that maritime cooperation should extend beyond the security framework to also cover areas like aquaculture, marine biotechnology, ocean science, protection and preservation of maritime environment and maritime tourism.
He also suggested that the two countries can explore the establishment of a joint Maritime Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) system involving relevant agencies for a coordinated and rapid response to natural calamities and man-made disasters.Rajnath also laid a wreath at the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) Memorial in Battaramulla and paid homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.

Necva Taştan Sevinç
09 September 2026•Update: 09 September 2026
Slovakia on Wednesday continued to block the extension of EU sanctions against Russia and demanded that certain individuals be removed from the bloc’s blacklist, according to media reports.
Bratislava reportedly opposed the renewal during a meeting of EU member states’ permanent representatives in Brussels, Italian news agency ANSA reported.
The EU’s 27 members have until Sept. 15 to reach an agreement before the sanctions expire.
The Committee of Permanent Representatives, known as Coreper, is expected to discuss the issue again before the deadline.
EU sanctions require the unanimous approval of all members and must be renewed periodically to remain in force.
Slovakia also earlier rejected a proposal to extend the sanctions regime for 12 months instead of six, reportedly becoming the only member state to oppose the plan.
The EU had sought a longer extension to avoid recurring negotiations about the measures.
Responding to the earlier dispute, the Slovak Foreign Ministry said discussions on the regular six-month review were continuing and were expected to be completed by Sept. 15.

Tate brothers lose bid for release from US jail pending extradition
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
16:27:58 UTC
01:27:58 KST

Tate brothers lose bid for release from US jail pending extradition
September 9 - Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate lost their bid for release from a Miami jail on Wednesday as they contest extradition to Britain, where they are wanted on rape charges.
Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis denied bail for the Tate brothers following a hearing last month in Miami federal court.
Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, were arrested in Miami on July 18 after Britain requested their extradition to face charges of rape, assault and facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. The Tate brothers, who have dual U.S. and British citizenship, have denied any wrongdoing.
The arrests marked a new phase in the legal troubles for the former kickboxers, who have built a large online following promoting their views on masculinity and wealth. Andrew Tate has previously described himself as a misogynist.
The Tates recruited dozens of women to work for a webcam pornography business starting in 2014, and later ran online courses called "Hustler's University," prosecutors with the Miami U.S. Attorney's office said in an August 10 court filing.
DEFENSE ARGUES AGAINST DETENTION
The prosecutors said there was a strong presumption in favor of detention in international extradition cases. They said the Tates could pose a danger to the community if released, citing British authorities' allegations that they strangled victims during forcible rapes, and that they could try to flee.
The prosecutors also pointed to allegations by authorities in Romania, where the brothers face human trafficking charges, that they sought to influence witnesses' statements while released on judicial supervision there. Romanian authorities say the Tates threatened to release private information about alleged victims and bribed an alleged victim, the U.S. prosecutors said.
The brothers' defense lawyers have said in court filings there was no need to keep them behind bars while the extradition process played out because their "extraordinary public visibility" would make it impractical for them to flee.
They argued the brothers had regularly appeared in court in Romania. They said the witnesses the Tates were alleged to have bribed were women who wanted to speak on their behalf, and said the Tates helped coordinate their travel to Bucharest and hired lawyers for them.
"The Tates’ compliance record is clear and convincing evidence they are not a danger to the community," the defense lawyers wrote.
The defense lawyers proposed that Louis release them on the conditions they post bond, surrender their passports and submit to location monitoring.
BRITISH CHARGES SPAN SEVEN YEARS
The legal process for determining whether the Tate brothers may be extradited could take months. Britain has until September 16 to submit its full extradition request to the State Department, U.S. court records show.
The impetus for the brothers' arrests in Miami was new charges brought by Britain's Crown Prosecution Service relating to alleged offenses involving four alleged victims between July 2010 and August 2017.
They had previously faced rape and human trafficking charges in Britain related to three alleged victims, the CPS said. A British judge issued a warrant for their arrests in 2024. They have not appeared in British court to enter a plea to those charges.
Britain is seeking to extradite the brothers to face both sets of charges. REUTERS
