Breadcrumb
John Malkovich bails on Israel performance following backlash, blames 'fake quotes'
John Malkovich has cancelled a planned visit to Israel amid online backlash, with the Hollywood actor blaming fabricated quotes attributed to him in Israeli media.
The 72-year-old actor had planned to travel to Tel Aviv in April 2027 for a one-off performance of The Music Critic, a satirical stage show that has toured dozens of countries around the world since 2021.
But in a statement on Tuesday, Malkovich announced he would no longer travel to the country after he was quoted praising Israel in local media.
An article published by The Jerusalem Post over the weekend quoted the actor as saying he was "thrilled to return to Israel" and expressing "strong closeness and solidarity" with Israeli people.
The announcement was met with backlash online, where social media users slammed the Oscar-winning actor's decision to travel to the country.
"I was made aware of an article which appeared in The Hollywood Reporter (first published in The Jerusalem Post) announcing a date in Tel Aviv, Israel, for a performance of a piece called 'The Music Critic,'" Malkovich said in a statement to Hollywood media.
"A PR company hired by the Israeli promoter drafted a quote for the article that was attributed to me, though I never made the statements that were quoted, nor was I consulted before they were printed. I did not utter these phrases, and they most certainly are not approved by me, nor do they reflect my feelings," he continued.
"The fact that they were printed as direct quotes from me is unacceptable and untenable. For this reason, I have decided I cannot participate in the Tel Aviv performance."
Malkovich has visited Israel several times during his decades-long career, once in 2008 as a guest of honour at the Jerusalem Film Festival and again in 2013 to perform The Infernal Comedy: Confessions of a Serial Killer at the Eilat International Chamber Music Festival and the Tel Aviv Museum of Art.
The visit had looked to be a rare show of public support for Israel from a major figure in Hollywood, where a cultural boycott has gathered pace in response to the genocide in Gaza and escalating violence in the occupied West Bank.
Thousands of actors, directors and film workers in 2025 vowed to cut ties with the Israeli film industry, which the Film Workers for Palestine said was "implicated in genocide and apartheid against the Palestinian people".

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026
China

Xinhua News Agency: We noted recent comments saying China only cares for its own development while “pulling up the ladder” for the development of other Global South countries. What is your comment?
Mao Ning: China never pulls up the ladder from any country. Rather, China has long been building up ladders so that countries could reach higher together. Through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, for instance, China has been helping partner countries bridge the infrastructure gap. By providing Global South countries with affordable industrial equipment and tech products and sharing experience and expertise, China has helped lower the cost for these countries’ industrial growth. China’s zero-tariff policy and “Export to China” initiative generate profits and market opportunities that enable Global South countries to better integrate into the global supply chains and enhance growth resilience.
For China, cooperation with other countries has always been about mutual success. The “pulling-up-the-ladder” narrative has zero resonance with Global South countries. China will always pursue mutual benefit and common development, be a reliable partner of Global South countries, and contribute to the prosperity of the Global South through China’s own development.
AFP: U.S. cyber security firm Calif said yesterday that it has built an AI-assisted hacking tool that can access the personal accounts and private information on the Chinese app WeChat. Tencent has said that the security risk has been fixed after being notified by Calif. But as a matter of cyber security, does the foreign ministry have comments on this?
Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China stands for promoting AI for good and preventing the abuse and malicious use of AI.
AFP: Yesterday, the U.S. Cyber Defense Agency accused top Chinese AI labs, including DeepSeek and Moonshot of stealing the capabilities of U.S. models. It said that these campaigns “form the core” of China-based AI companies’ strategies. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this?
Mao Ning: The development of AI in China comes from greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and is fueled by China’s vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit and commitment to open cooperation. We believe all parties need to make sure AI development is open and inclusive and promotes the well-being of humanity as a force for good and for all. We hope the U.S. side will earnestly act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and stop leveling false allegations to smear China. As two major powers in AI, China and the U.S. should step up cooperation.
NHK: The BRICS Summit will be held in India this weekend. Who will lead the Chinese delegation?
Mao Ning: We will release timely information if there is any update. Please stay tuned.
AFP: At an international forum yesterday, the Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilberto Teodoro Jr. criticized what he called a violation of UNCLOS and “coercion, bullying and aggression” by China in response to him being handed a piece of paper stating China’s position on the South China Sea. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on the situation or a response to the remarks by the Philippines’ Defense Secretary?
Mao Ning: I’m not sure what exactly happened at the event, but China’s position has always been clear on the so-called “South China Sea arbitration”. The Philippines unilaterally initiated the case, which is a distortion and abuse of the UNCLOS dispute settlement mechanism. It is the Philippine side who has violated UNCLOS and undermined its integrity and authority.
We urge the certain individual of the Philippine side to cut the provocations and theatrics, and stop undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea.

Finland says GNSS jamming, wind caused Ukrainian drones to enter its airspace in spring
HELSINKI, Sept 9 - Four Ukrainian military drones found in Finland in March and April were diverted from their intended route by satellite navigation interference in combination with wind, Finnish police and border guards said on Wednesday.
Finland and nearby Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania have seen a string of recent incidents where Ukrainian drones aimed at Russia have strayed into their airspace.
• "The investigation established that the UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) originated in Ukraine and formed part of Ukraine's countermeasures in response to Russia's war of aggression," the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement.
• "The UAVs had not, however, been targeted at Finland; instead, they were thrown off course by strong GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) jamming detected in the eastern Gulf of Finland at the time, combined with the prevailing weather conditions," it added.
• The agencies said the prosecutor had closed the investigations into the incidents, having found no grounds to pursue criminal liability.
• The agencies said all four drones had carried explosives. No injuries or property damage were reported in connection with the crashes. REUTERS

'One in six attacks': Israel was most targeted nation by hacktivism campaigns in first half of 2026
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:22:05 UTC
19:22:05 KST

Israel was the world’s top target for hacktivist attacks in the first half of 2026, with one in six attacks targeting the Jewish state, the Radware H1 2026 Global Threat Report revealed on Wednesday.
Hacktivist attacks are carried out by non-state actors, often sponsored by states but not officially part of their organization, against selected countries for geopolitical reasons.
According to the report, Israel absorbed 16% of all the hacktivist campaigns, with 784 recorded reports of attacks; the United States was second with 8%, and the United Kingdom was third, while many European countries supporting Ukraine in the war against Russia absorbed a significant number of secondary attacks.
The report noted that a spike in attacks of this style was recorded during the US and Israel war against Iran, after hacktivist attacks hit a record low during the first months of the year.
In comparison to previous years, the first half of 2026 has been one of the periods with the lowest number of hack attacks recorded, with the peak of hacktivism attacks being reached after the October 7 massacre and the beginning of the Israel-Hamas War, the report said.
“The most significant finding is not merely that Israel once again ranks first but that the gap between it and the other countries continues to widen,” Ron Meyran, vice president of Cyber Intelligence at Radware, said.
“The digital arena has become an inseparable part of every military conflict, and the campaign against Iran demonstrated how quickly dozens of groups can mobilize and act against organizations in Israel,” Meyran added.
Most hacktivist groups active in the first half of the year were from the pro-Russia, anti-Western collective, with 85% of such attacks claimed by groups in the collective, the report added. The most active group was NoName057, which accounted for almost 40% of the attacks.
Targeting infrastructure, autonomous systems
It also noted that the attacks centered on infrastructure, with the main targets being industrial facilities that provide essential services and whose disruption could pressure public officials.
According to the findings, 37% of the attacks targeted governmental institutions, while other targets were against manufacturing services (8%), business (7%), hospitality (6%), and the financial sector (5%).
In terms of the services targeted, the main objective was to disrupt autonomous system numbers (ASNs); the main companies affected by those attacks were Microsoft (22%), Amazon Web Services (13%), and Google Cloud Platform (7%).
Secondary targets included several European hosting providers, notably Hetzner Online (8.4%), because their infrastructure is key to supporting Ukrainian and Israeli networks, such as uPress, Radware, Hosting Ukraine, and Cellcom.

6 potato pancake recipes that everyone can make
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
13:21:43 EEST
19:21:43 KST

6 potato pancake recipes that everyone can make
Kyiv • UNN
UNN presents six potato pancake recipes: classic, with meat, cheese, mushrooms, liver, and without flour or eggs.
Deruny are a simple potato dish that can be diversified with various fillings and additional ingredients. UNN has compiled the top 6 best recipes, among which there is an option to suit every taste.
Classic deruny
Ingredients:
-  potatoes - 1 kg; 
-  onions - 2; 
-  eggs - 2; 
-  flour - 30 g; 
-  garlic - 2 cloves; 
-  salt - to taste; 
-  ground black pepper - to taste; 
-  oil - for frying. 
Preparation:
Peel the potatoes and grate them. Add the grated onion and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Add the minced garlic, eggs, flour, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Heat a frying pan with oil. Spoon the potato mixture into the pan, forming small pancakes.
Fry the deruny for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Serve hot with sour cream.
Deruny with meat filling
Ingredients:
-  potatoes - 1 kg; 
-  onion - 1 large; 
-  eggs - 2; 
-  flour - 4 tbsp.; 
-  ground meat - 400 g; 
-  salt - to taste; 
-  pepper - to taste; 
-  oil - for frying. 
Preparation:
Peel the potatoes, grate them on a fine grater, and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Grate the onion on a fine grater as well.
Mix the potatoes and onion, then add the eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Prepare the ground meat in advance. Chicken can be used raw, while beef or pork is recommended to be fried beforehand until partially cooked.
Spoon the potato mixture onto a preheated frying pan. Place some ground meat in the center and cover it with another layer of potatoes.
Fry over medium heat for approximately 4 minutes on each side.
Place the finished deruny on a paper towel.
Deruny with cheese
Ingredients:
-  potatoes - 1 kg; 
-  onion - 1; 
-  eggs - 2; 
-  flour - 50 g; 
-  hard or semi-hard cheese - 100 g; 
-  garlic - 2 cloves; 
-  salt - to taste; 
-  ground black pepper - to taste; 
-  oil - for frying. 
Preparation:
Squeeze the grated potatoes and onion to remove the excess liquid, leaving the starch.
Add the grated cheese, eggs, flour, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Mix all the ingredients.
Spoon the mixture into a preheated frying pan with oil.
Fry for 3-4 minutes on each side.
Deruny with mushrooms
Ingredients:
-  potatoes - 1 kg; 
-  onions - 2; 
-  eggs - 2; 
-  flour - 100 g; 
-  sour cream - 150 g; 
-  champignons or seasonal mushrooms - 300 g; 
-  salt - to taste; 
-  ground black pepper - to taste; 
-  oil - for frying. 
Preparation:
Grate the potatoes and onions on a fine grater.
Add the flour, sour cream, salt, and pepper, and mix.
Add the eggs and mix well again.
Cut the mushrooms into small pieces and fry them.
Add the mushrooms to the potato mixture.
Fry the deruny in a preheated frying pan with oil on both sides until golden brown.
Serve with sour cream or yogurt sauce.
Liver deruny
Ingredients:
-  chicken liver - 300 g; 
-  onion - 1; 
-  carrot - 1; 
-  potato - 1; 
-  sour cream - 2 tbsp.; 
-  egg - 1; 
-  flour - 3 tbsp.; 
-  salt - 1 tsp.; 
-  black pepper - ½ tsp.; 
-  dried garlic - ½ tsp.; 
-  oil - for frying. 
Preparation:
Finely chop the liver.
Add the chopped onion, grated carrot, and potato.
Add the egg, salt, pepper, and dried garlic.
Add the flour and sour cream, and mix.
Heat a frying pan with oil.
Spoon the mixture into the pan, forming deruny.
Fry on both sides until browned.
Deruny without flour or eggs
Ingredients:
-  potatoes - 700 g; 
-  sunflower oil -60 ml; 
-  butter - 15 g; 
-  salt - 1 tsp.; 
-  ground black pepper - to taste. 
Preparation:
Peel the potatoes and grate them on a coarse grater.
Cover them with cold water and rinse several times until the water becomes almost clear.
Drain the potatoes in a colander and squeeze them thoroughly through a clean towel. The mixture should remain as dry as possible.
Add the salt and pepper immediately before frying.
Heat a wide frying pan, then add the oil and butter.
Add the potatoes in small portions and form thin deruny.
Fry over medium heat for 4-5 minutes on each side.
Place the finished deruny on a paper towel and serve hot with sour cream, yogurt sauce, or fresh herbs.

19:17:04 KST

MOSCOW, September 9. /TASS/. Pressure from imported products, including those from China and Kazakhstan, on the Russian rolled steel market persists, although the overall situation remains stable and predictable. At the same time, competition in the finished products segment has intensified due to an influx of low-quality products, Director of Severstal Distribution (part of Severstal) Viktor Romanovsky told reporters.
"If we talk about import pressure on the Russian market, it still persists," Romanovsky said in response to a question about competition from Chinese and Kazakh imports. He added that some local players had redirected their volumes to other markets, but their share was not large enough to significantly reduce the overall pressure.
According to Romanovsky, the situation is more challenging in the finished products segment. "If we talk about competition in finished products, the situation here has definitely not improved and may even have worsened," he said. Romanovsky stressed that despite efforts by Russian producers and their customers to reduce costs and improve efficiency, large volumes of low-quality products continue to enter the market.
"And customers whose purchasing power is declining often choose price over quality, sometimes disregarding the quality characteristics of the product itself," Romanovsky added, explaining the reasons for increased competition in this segment.
Last summer, Severstal CEO Alexander Shevelev said that rising steel imports into Russia were increasing the market's sensitivity, although imports were not yet particularly painful for Russian steelmakers. Severstal is analyzing the situation and does not rule out initiating anti-dumping duties.
Severstal is a vertically integrated mining and steel company and one of Russia's largest steel producers. The company's key asset is the Cherepovets Steel Mill, which has an annual production capacity of around 12 mln metric tons of steel. Severstal's largest shareholder is Alexey Mordashov, who owns approximately 77.03% of the company's shares.

Google to invest €13bn in Finnish AI data centres, its biggest European push yet
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:16:43 UTC
19:16:43 KST

Google will spend at least €13 billion on data centres and digital infrastructure in Finland over the next two years, its largest single investment in Europe, in a bet on the country's cheap power and climate.
Helsinki has landed the biggest cheque Google has written anywhere in Europe
The company announced on Wednesday that a €13 billion investment will fund data centres and supporting infrastructure across four municipalities, along with clean energy projects and funds dedicated to local biodiversity, education, research and workforce development.
The facilities in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala will power a range of Google services, among them its Gemini chatbot. The company described the decision as "a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure."
Construction is expected across 2027 and 2028, and the firm estimates the investment will add €3.6 billion a year to Finland's GDP while supporting more than 37,000 jobs, roughly 16,000 of them in construction.
Once the building stops, Google projects the sites will sustain around 7,000 jobs annually, spanning technical and facility roles, equipment suppliers, as well as the shops, restaurants and services used by those workers and their families.
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo welcomed the announcement in Google's statement.
"Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths. The value of the data economy extends far beyond direct investment into spurring innovation, research and development," Orpo said, adding that closer collaboration would "deliver lasting benefits for both parties."
Why Finland
The appeal to invest in Finland is rooted in its cold climate.
Data centres generate enormous heat and consume vast quantities of electricity, and Finland offers a cold climate that reduces cooling costs alongside relatively cheap and stable power from nuclear plants, wind and hydro.
That combination has produced a boom, with dozens of data centres already under construction across the country.
Google's own presence dates back to 2009, when it bought a disused paper mill in the coastal city of Hamina and converted it, expanding steadily since.
For Orpo's right-wing government, attracting this kind of investment has also been a priority, especially since Finnish elections will take place in April of next year.
Finland is contending with record unemployment and weak growth, and the data economy has become one of the few sectors offering the prospect of substantial investment and job creation.

Poor condition of Baltic Sea behind flounder population slump
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:15:00 UTC
19:15:00 KST

Poor condition of Baltic Sea behind flounder population slump
Although fishers attribute the low abundance of flounder to the spread of an invasive species, a fisheries scientist says the cause is the Baltic Sea's poor hydrological conditions.
According to Taavi Suitsberg, chairman of the NGO Lääne County Coastal Fisheries Association and a professional fisherman, fishers believe the decline in flounder numbers is due to the invasive round goby, which competes with native fish species for food and reproduces more quickly.
At the same time, Suitsberg said the growing number of gobies is a double-edged sword for fishers. Although they are said to be crowding out flounder species, gobies are themselves edible fish and serve as food for larger fish.
However, Suitsberg acknowledged that he could not say exactly why flounder numbers are declining and that fishers had also learned about the possible impact of the invasive species from scientists.
Redik Eschbaum, head of the coastal fisheries working group at the University of Tartu's Estonian Marine Institute's Department of Fish Biology and Fisheries, said aquatic ecosystems are so complex that it is difficult to pinpoint a single cause for a species' decline.
However, Eschbaum confirmed that a lack of food cannot be the direct cause, as researchers have not found emaciated flounder. Flounder numbers were also already low before the round goby became widespread, all of which points to hydrological conditions as the cause.
According to Eschbaum, cod are in an even worse situation than flounder. Like flounder, their spawning depends on inflows of saltwater. Cod fishing is banned altogether in the Baltic Sea.
One thing flounder and cod have in common is pelagic eggs, meaning their eggs float freely in the water rather than sticking to underwater plants or objects. These species spawn in deeper, saltier layers of water where their eggs also develop.
Eschbaum said there are two possible reasons why spawning has become more difficult for these species. First, decomposing algae on the seabed may be leaving too little oxygen there.
Another possibility is that climate change has altered wind patterns. "Saltwater inflows are no longer as extensive and don't occur at the same time of year as they used to. But the fish have no way of anticipating that," Eschbaum said.
Eschbaum said that historically, two types of flounder were distinguished in the Baltic Sea: deepwater-spawning flounder and coastal-spawning flounder. It was later discovered, however, that they are two entirely separate species.
Although Baltic Sea flounder are a good example of rapid evolution, the two species have adapted differently. Coastal-spawning flounder, for example, are faring somewhat better, although they too would benefit from saltier water.
Although Eschbaum said flounder numbers are not expected to increase in the near future, the species cannot be considered endangered.

Ukraine's KORT unveils Hunter Killer line of mid- and long-range attack drones – photos
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
13:14:00 EEST
19:14:00 KST

Ukraine's KORT unveils Hunter Killer line of mid- and long-range attack drones – photos
KORT, a Ukrainian drone and component manufacturer, has unveiled its Hunter Killer line of UAVs, comprising mid- and long-range one-way attack drones.
Source: Ukrainska Pravda at the MSPO-2026 exhibition in Poland
Details: The unveiled line includes aircraft of various types with warheads weighing between three and 70 kg.
A KORT representative told Ukrainska Pravda: "We currently have four versions of aircraft with different modifications and different warheads on display. We are also working on larger long-range attack drones and mid-range attack drones equipped with pusher engines, meaning the propeller is located at the rear of the drone. This change in the design is being made at the request of the military to increase the chances of hitting armoured targets."
The mid-range strike line starts with the Hunter Killer 3. This fixed-wing drone was developed based on the Ardea reconnaissance drone. The company is presenting three versions of the Hunter Killer 3 with take-off weights of 10, 10.5 and 14 kg.
Depending on the modification, the aircraft can remain airborne for 60 to 140 minutes and cover distances of 100 to 250 km. Its warhead weighs 3 kg. Radio communications or Starlink are used for control. The drones are also equipped with thermal imaging cameras and an automatic navigation system.
The more advanced line consists of the Hunter Killer S, 10M, 15S, 15M, 15 and 20 models. They can be used as either mid-range or long-range attack drones.
The Hunter Killer S, 10M, 15S and 15M are mid-range attack drones. They have a stated range of up to 300 km and can carry a warhead weighing up to 15 kg. The models differ in fuselage design and communications systems. The Hunter Killer S and Hunter Killer 15S use Starlink, while the other models in this group are equipped with radio communications.
The Hunter Killer 15 and 20 are long-range attack drones. According to the company, they can cover up to 700 km and carry a warhead weighing up to 10 kg. The models also have different fuselage designs.
The most advanced models in the line, the Hunter Killer 50S and 70, are at the final testing stage. The Hunter Killer 50S is a mid-range attack drone with a 60-kg warhead and a range of up to 600 km. The Hunter Killer 70 is a long-range attack drone with a 50-kg warhead and a range of up to 1,200 km. The company is also developing a 70-kg warhead.
The two latest models are distinguished by interchangeable wings that allow the range to be extended by increasing the wing area. The fuselage remains unchanged.
The long-range strike versions of the Hunter Killer drones are also equipped with an eight-channel CRPA antenna manufactured by KORT. It is designed to ensure the aircraft can navigate in conditions of electronic warfare.
Earlier, at the MSPO exhibition in Poland, Ukraine also presented, for the first time, an anti-aircraft missile for the Osa surface-to-air missile system as well as a new version of the Vilkha missile.

Republicans tie midterm hopes to Trump, calling Democrats 'dangerous, radical and weird'
DALLAS, Sept 9 - Republicans opened their unusual midterm convention on Wednesday by portraying Democrats as "dangerous" and "extreme" while praising President Donald Trump's record, making a risky bet that the president can energize core backers despite his broad unpopularity.
The two-day gathering underscores the extent to which Republicans' fortunes are tethered to Trump and serves as a showcase for their strategy ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
The event is so centered on the president that Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters informally dubbed it "Trumpapalooza," a nod to the popular Lollapalooza music festival.
Many Republicans in competitive House and Senate races skipped the convention, underscoring concerns within the party that Trump's appeal to loyal supporters may not be enough to overcome voter dissatisfaction over inflation and the war on Iran.
Those in Dallas who took the stage early on Wednesday unleashed a stream of invective aimed at Democrats, offering political red meat to diehard Republicans by going after Democrats over issues such as transgender women in sports and border security.
Many called Democrats "socialists" and "communists," echoing one of Trump's favorite attack lines following a handful of victories by democratic socialists in Democratic primary elections.
Democrats are "dangerous, radical and weird," said Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the party's Senate campaign arm.
Wednesday's program also featured a surprise video from Democratic U.S. Senator John Fetterman, who introduced his Republican colleague from Pennsylvania, Senator Dave McCormick, as his "great friend" while declaring he would work with Trump to protect the state's steel industry.
The virtual appearance appeared likely to emphasize the ideological divides plaguing the Democratic Party ahead of the midterms. Fetterman has denied speculation that he may leave the party.
The stakes are high for both parties. With the elections less than two months away, Republicans face the prospect of losing control of at least one chamber of Congress, with public polling showing Democrats more motivated to vote and Trump's approval ratings deeply underwater.
With no official party business on the agenda, the gathering resembled a Trump campaign rally more than a traditional party convention, which is held every four years to nominate presidential and vice presidential candidates.
Trump will speak both nights, delivering the keynote address on Wednesday and then offering the last word after Vice President JD Vance speaks on Thursday evening. In his remarks, Gruters described Trump as the "greatest president" in U.S. history and the "greatest Republican messenger of our lifetime."
At least 16 candidates in competitive House and Senate races were scheduled to speak, according to the RNC's schedule. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a close Trump ally who is locked in a tough Senate race with Democratic lawmaker James Talarico, delivered a brief speech on Wednesday.
Those staying away include Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan and Senator Susan Collins of Maine, both facing strong Democratic challengers this fall.
The party that controls the White House historically loses congressional seats in midterm elections, and Trump's popularity has sagged as the Iran war and his tariff regime have increased energy costs and consumer prices.
A CHANCE TO RALLY THE BASE
The convention will face stiff competition for viewers with the start of the NFL season, with opening night coinciding with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks and Thursday's program overlapping with a matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams.
Still, after months of negative headlines over the Iran war and inflation, many Republicans see the gathering as their best chance to promote candidates, draw contrasts with Democrats on affordability, immigration and healthcare, and energize a Republican electorate expressing less enthusiasm about voting than Democrats, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
Trump cabinet members who will address the gathering include Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose comments are likely to be closely watched amid concerns about the growing U.S. debt and high cost of living.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries dispatched four Democratic lawmakers to Dallas as part of the party's counter-programming effort.
"Americans are drowning in the failed Republican economy," Jeffries said in a statement. "Rather than taking a single step to lower costs, MAGA extremists are partying with their super-rich donors in Dallas." REUTERS

Beyazıt State Library to undergo restoration, collection temporarily moved
Unknown

2026-09-09

19:11:00 KST

Inside of the historic Beyazıt State Library (AA Photo)
The historic Beyazıt State Library, one of Istanbul’s oldest cultural institutions, will undergo extensive restoration and earthquake reinforcement, with its collection temporarily relocated during the works, the Culture and Tourism Ministry has said.
The announcement came in response to reports that the nearly 150-year-old library would be closed. The ministry’s General Directorate of Libraries and Publications stressed that the institution would not be shut down and that library services would continue throughout the restoration period.
The library’s books and periodicals will be transferred to designated areas at the Halkalı Library Complex, currently under construction in Istanbul’s Küçükçekmece district. Planned as one of the city’s largest library facilities, the complex will have about 30,000 square meters of usable space.
The temporary relocation is intended to protect the collection while ensuring continued public access. In addition, users will be able to access approximately 25 million digitized images of Beyazıt State Library’s books and periodicals through digital infrastructure being established at the Istanbul Orhan Kemal Provincial Public Library.
The Halkalı complex will also serve as a new technical center for the library system. Facilities for bookbinding, conservation and digitization will be established, allowing previously unbound periodicals to be completed and preserved, deteriorated works to be restored, and materials in the Beyazıt collection to be digitized.
According to the ministry, the facilities will continue to serve libraries across Istanbul after the historic collection returns to Beyazıt, providing technical and logistical support to institutions throughout the city.
The restoration will focus on preserving the historic character of the Beyazıt building while strengthening it against earthquake risks. Once the work is completed, the collection will be returned to its historic home.
The ministry said the renovated library will reopen with modern services and improved access facilities.

FACTBOX – BRICS summit in India: Who’s attending and what’s on the agenda
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:10:49 UTC
19:10:49 KST

- Leaders from across Asia, Africa, Middle East, Latin America expected to attend including China's Xi, Russia's Putin and Iran's Pezeshkian
- Agenda could include Iran-US conflict, de-dollarization, India-China relations
BRICS leaders will gather in the Indian capital New Delhi this weekend for a two-day summit as the expanded grouping seeks to strengthen its role in global political and economic affairs.
The 18th edition of the BRICS Leaders’ Summit, scheduled for Sept. 12-13 and hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, will bring leaders together from across Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America.
Who is attending?
Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are among the leaders expected to attend.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are also expected to be there.
The expanded BRICS membership comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates.
The group has also partner countries, including Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam joining the framework.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed are also expected to attend.
Cuba, Nigeria and Uzbekistan are likely to be represented by their presidents, Miguel Diaz-Canel, Bola Tinubu and Shavkat Mirziyoyev, respectively.
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is also expected to attend.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is expected to be represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, while the UAE is expected to send Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in place of President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
Agenda and key points
The agenda is generally expected to focus on trade, development financing and reform of global institutions.
However, the summit comes amid the conflict between Iran and the US, and its broader impact on the global economy, including an energy crisis that has particularly affected Asia. The issue is therefore likely to emerge as a major point of discussion among members.
Iran may push for a summit declaration reflecting its position on the conflict, while the organization requires full consensus to reach an agreement.
The summit could also provide an important backdrop for India and China’s complex relationship.
If Chinese President Xi attends, it would be his first visit to India since his 2019 informal summit with Prime Minister Modi.
The two countries are among the world’s largest economies and are major BRICS members, but their relationship continues to be shaped by unresolved border and sovereignty disputes.
Eerishika Pankaj of Australia’s Lowy Institute has described BRICS and the India-China strategic dialogue as institutional mechanisms that allow the two sides to maintain communication despite their differences.
“Cooperation and unresolved sovereignty disputes coexist,” Pankaj wrote, arguing that BRICS should be viewed as a means of maintaining dialogue rather than evidence that India and China have resolved their disagreements.
Beyond bilateral issues, BRICS is also expected to address reform of global institutions, an issue the bloc has repeatedly raised in relation to institutions such as the UN, IMF and World Bank.
De-dollarization
Another key area of BRICS cooperation has been the use of national currencies in trade and finance, reflecting efforts by members to reduce their dependence on the US dollar.
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said last year that BRICS member states were increasingly adopting local-currency settlements in bilateral financial transactions as part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on foreign currencies and strengthen economic cooperation within the group.
However, despite discussions about expanding local-currency settlements in trade, members have stopped short of establishing a common BRICS currency.
The New Development Bank, the bloc’s multilateral development bank, has also made local-currency financing a strategic priority.
According to its 2024 report, 43.5% of its approvals that year were denominated in member countries’ currencies, primarily the South African rand and Chinese yuan.
A short history of BRICS
As these leaders gather in New Delhi, their meeting underscores the bloc’s dramatic expansion since its creation in 2006.
BRIC was formalized at a meeting of foreign ministers on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York in 2006, bringing together Brazil, Russia, India and China.
The first leaders’ summit of the then BRIC was held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009.
South Africa joined in 2010, transforming BRIC into BRICS. The grouping subsequently underwent another major expansion, bringing in countries from the Middle East and Africa and, most recently, Indonesia.
According to figures cited by BRICS, the grouping now represents about 49.5% of the world’s population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade.
BRICS describes itself as a platform for consultation and cooperation on global and regional issues, including international political and economic governance.
The last BRICS summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 2025 while China is due to host the 2027 summit.

More schools close in Indonesia as haze worsens
Schools in Palembang switch to remote learning as haze from forest and peatland fires pushes air pollution to unhealthy levels
Schools in the capital of Indonesia’s South Sumatra province switched to remote learning on Wednesday as worsening haze from forest and peatland fires pushed air pollution to unhealthy levels, adding to disruptions that had already affected more than 1.4 million students across the country, officials said.
Indonesia has been plagued by forest and land fires for decades but an intensifying El Nino pattern and a prolonged dry season made the impact of the fires especially dire this year. Toxic haze and smoke have spread far beyond Indonesia’s borders in Southeast Asia, creating a regional health crisis.
The smoke has drifted as far as the Philippines, more than 800km (500 miles) away, and breached Malaysia’s emergency-level threshold, forcing authorities to declare an emergency last week in a town in Sarawak state on Borneo Island.
In Palembang, the capital city of South Sumatra province, schools from kindergarten to junior high were ordered to start conducting classes online on Wednesday under an emergency measure.
Mayor Ratu Dewa said the thickening smoke posed health risks to children, including acute respiratory infections.
“Students’ health and safety remained the government’s priority,” Dewa said. Teachers were also asked to avoid excessive assignments during the period of remote learning, he added.
The policy, affecting more than 250,000 students at 1,030 schools in Palembang, would be reviewed regularly, and in-person classes will resume once conditions improve, he said.

Kiev wants advance Patriot shipments against unbought missiles
Ukraine wants its Western donors to supply highly sought-after Patriot interceptors from their own stockpiles, which would be replenished later with 1,000 missiles that Kiev plans to purchase with EU money.
The unorthodox proposal was outlined on Tuesday by Ukrainian Defense Minister Evgeny Khmara during a video call with Western arms donors. It comes amid a global shortage of US-made weapons, with Ukraine competing for supplies against numerous other countries while arguing that its need to intercept Russian ballistic missiles should take priority.
Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky previously sought to secure 300 Patriot interceptors for the upcoming winter. His reported effort to impress US President Donald Trump with long-range strikes on Russian refineries and e-commerce warehouses has produced no clear results.
The attacks were allegedly intended to persuade Trump to approve additional Patriot supplies. Kiev also overspent Western donor funds while pursuing the strategy and has a $27 billion military budget deficit.
Speaking to members of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, Khmara said his country is contracting 1,000 Patriot missiles “through the EU loan,” but acknowledged that the purchase does not resolve the immediate shortage.
“The majority of these missiles will only start to be shipped in the coming years, which is why we ask that you supply us the missiles from your stockpiles today in exchange for future improved missiles from our contracts,” he said.
German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said at the same meeting that Berlin is working to provide additional Patriot interceptors of the older PAC-2 model from its own stocks, along with air-to-air missiles that Ukraine uses against Russian drones and cruise missiles, including from Western-donated F-16 fighter jets.
Western Europe’s purse remains open for Kiev
The meeting, co-chaired by Pistorius and British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting, coincided with announcements from both the EU and the UK regarding their respective aid programs.
Together with @SecGenNATO Rutte, I welcome the agreement by Member States on the derogation for Ukraine to purchase crucial products for Patriot air defence systems.
The next disbursement of €3.2 billion will enable Ukraine to better protect its skies from Russia’s…
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the disbursement of €3.2 billion ($3.7 billion) under the Ukraine Support Loan mechanism, saying the funds “will enable Ukraine to better protect its skies.”
The British government pledged a £100 million ($136 million) “winter air defense package,” with the money slated to be spent on US-made weapons through NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) program.
Trump’s mediation efforts renewed
Trump has sought to distance the US from the Ukraine conflict, arguing that European NATO members should bear more of the burden of the prolonged hostilities with Russia. Last week, his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow and Kiev as part of an effort to revive US-mediated peace talks.
The latest US proposal contains “worse” terms for Ukraine than those previously on the table, according to Ukrainian MP Anna Skorokhod. Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska in August 2025 to discuss a possible off-ramp in the conflict, but Zelensky rejected key terms sought by Moscow.
In June, Zelensky announced a 40-day “pressure campaign” involving an escalation of long-range attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and trade. Moscow retaliated with strikes that left Ukrainian ports effectively cut off from maritime routes.

Top EU court throws out Orban-era attempt to block funds for Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:09:19 UTC
19:09:19 KST

Editor's Note: This article has been updated with comments from the European Union Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
The EU's Court of Justice on Sept. 9 dismissed a legal challenge filed by former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban intended to prevent money linked to frozen Russian assets from being spent on the EU's military aid to Ukraine.
EU countries agreed in EU 2024 to bankroll some military assistance for Ukraine using the interest generated on Russian government assets that have been "frozen" within the EU since Moscow launched its 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Orban's Hungary in August 2025 sought to challenge the legality of the procedure that provided for the European Peace Facility — an EU instrument for providing security assistance to partner countries — to support Ukraine in this way.
However, the Luxembourg-based Court of Justice has thrown out the action as "it does not fall within the jurisdiction of the EU judicature."
"We welcome the judgement of the General Court, which confirmed the limits of judicial review in Common Foreign and Security Policy," Christian Wigand, EU Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, told the Kyiv Independent.
"The decision of the European Peace Facility Committee concerned the Union's strategic or political choices and therefore fell outside the Court's jurisdiction under its case-law. This judgment means that the support already granted to Ukraine has not been called into question."
Agreements concluded by EU member states under the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) generally do not fall within the court's remit.
The European Peace Facility is generally funded by direct contributions from EU countries and was established to help prevent conflict and provide non-lethal aid.
Its scope was expanded in light of the full-scale invasion to provide direct lethal aid to Ukraine, and it has provided Kyiv with 11.1 billion euros ($13 billion) of support since 2022.
However, Orban undermined the peace facility's effectiveness not only through legal challenges but also by blocking the reimbursement mechanism for EU countries purchasing equipment for Ukraine.
That issue has remained blocked even after Orban was voted out of office in April 2026, because of differences of opinion over how much to reimburse old contributions versus provide fresh support to Ukraine.
However, the EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said at a meeting of EU defense ministers on Sept. 1 that agreement was close.
"I think it's very clear that there is a determination to unlock the European Peace Facility, and that's something that we will work on very closely," Kallas said.
The current Hungarian prime minister, Peter Magyar, has not spoken about the European Peace Facility case but has adopted a more constructive approach to relations with the EU since taking office in May.
While Magyar has repeatedly ruled out his country providing direct military assistance to Ukraine, he has affirmed Kyiv's right to defend itself and signaled Budapest would not obstruct assistance from other EU members.

The war in the Gulf will have to end in compromise
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:09:04 UTC
19:09:04 KST

The war in the Gulf will have to end in compromise
The US and Israel have not achieved their original objectives, Iran has not surrendered and the costs are spreading across the region.
The current Gulf war does not look like other wars. Conflicts, whether short or prolonged, usually end in one of two ways. Either one side achieves a decisive victory over the other, typically followed by the signing of a surrender agreement and the imposition of the victor’s terms on the defeated party, as happened in the first and second world wars, both of which ended in Allied victory. Or such wars end in a settlement based on the principle of “no victor and no vanquished”, with each side throwing the full extent of its military capabilities into battle against the other. Both sides are exhausted without either achieving a decisive result, at which point they move to end the fighting and reach a settlement that takes their interests into account. The war then ends almost as though it had never begun, apart from the human and material losses it caused.
One example is the Iran-Iraq war, which lasted eight years without either Iran or Iraq achieving its objectives. Iraq did not liberate Arabistan, and Iran did not succeed in overthrowing Iraq’s Baath Party regime.
Looking at America’s modern wars, the truth is that it has not won any of them. It may not have been defeated, but it did not achieve the objectives for which those wars were fought. The image of the helicopter evacuations from Saigon remains vivid, as does the historic scene at Kabul airport, when America’s allies clung desperately to a lifeline, to no avail.
In the Vietnam War, the Americans lost nearly 60,000 military personnel. The result was an agreement in Paris to end the war and provide the United States with a way out, amid a clear Vietnamese victory. The Americans withdrew from Vietnam and the country was unified on Vietnamese terms.
The same was true of the US war in Afghanistan. Thousands of tonnes of bombs were dropped on the country, only for the United States to withdraw suddenly and chaotically, in scenes that resembled an escape from disaster. Then there was the US invasion of Iraq, where the war seemed almost to have been fought on Iran’s behalf. What Tehran had been unable to achieve during the eight-year war, America achieved for it by handing Iraq over to Iran. America may lose wars, but it does not learn from them before starting another.
Today, the current Gulf war is strange and falls outside both of these familiar patterns. Last year, we were surprised by a US-Israeli war on Iran that lasted a little less than two weeks, with the aim of eliminating Iran’s nuclear programme. Yet it suddenly stopped. US warships departed, and Israeli aircraft left the skies above Tehran without dropping their payloads, following a decision by the US president. Both sides claimed victory, despite the fact that the objective of the war had not been achieved.
Things remained unchanged for months before the war suddenly resumed. At the time, the Americans and Iranians were engaged in negotiations mediated by Oman, and talks between the parties were supposed to resume just one day after the start of massive military operations: relentless bombardment from US warships and Israeli aircraft flying around the clock over Iranian cities.
The second surprise was that this war, too, stopped without warning, ushering in a period of threats that fighting would resume: US and Israeli threats met by Iranian threats, and an intermittent war in which an American strike is answered by an Iranian one, and so on. Israel, the occupying state, has meanwhile been kept out of this contest of wills.
This, then, is not a war like other wars. It resembles a cockfight. Nor is it being fought according to the principle of “no victor and no vanquished”. Both sides continue to claim that they possess the will and the ability to fight.
On the battlefield, every American strike is met by an Iranian strike, even if the Iranian response has less impact. But this means that the Iranians have not surrendered, that their resolve has not weakened and that they still retain a relative capacity to confront their adversary.
Turning to President Trump’s decision to maintain the blockade on Iran and tighten the economic sanctions he has described as devastating and unprecedented, it is worth remembering that sanctions have been imposed on Iran for more than 40 years.
This invites comparison with the sanctions and blockade imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait, which led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands amid shortages of food and medicine and impoverished Iraqis to the point that they sold their most valuable possessions simply to meet the costs of everyday life.
The blockade and sanctions therefore had an enormous impact on the lives of Iraqis. But is Iran’s situation comparable with Iraq’s? I believe it is entirely different, and the comparison is inaccurate. Iran is several times the size of Iraq. Iraq was surrounded by countries hostile to its political regime, including Iran and Syria. Its only lifeline was Jordan, which was itself constrained at the port of Aqaba to prevent any breach of the blockade.
Iran’s situation is different. It has extensive borders with several countries, including Pakistan, Afghanistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan and Iraq. There is no clear hostility between Iran and these states that would lead them to tighten the blockade or adhere rigidly to US sanctions. Iraq, in fact, amounts to an open border through which Iran can obtain whatever it needs.
More importantly still, Iran has a coastline of roughly 700 kilometres on the Caspian Sea, which opens onto several countries, most notably Russia, which shares the sea with Iran and maintains good relations with Tehran. For this reason, I do not believe that the blockade and sanctions, however severe they become, will force the Iranians to back down or surrender.
In my view, if the Iranians were given a choice between surrender and fighting another war, they might choose war. They still appear to possess a degree of strength and perhaps the ability to rebuild their capabilities as well.
In conclusion, the objectives behind this US-Israeli war on Iran were to end Iran’s nuclear programme, eliminate its missile system or at least limit its range, and overthrow the regime. None of these three objectives has been achieved. It is true that the supreme leader and many Iranian leaders have been killed, that large parts of the country’s infrastructure have been destroyed and that Iran’s military capabilities have been weakened. Despite all this, the current Iranian leadership has become more hardline than its predecessors.
What is striking is the issue of freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. It was not a direct cause of the outbreak of war, but it has become one of its consequences. It is almost as though the US-Israeli objectives of the war had been achieved, even though they have not. Restoring freedom of navigation through the strait has now become the urgent priority, in order to prevent a global rise in oil prices and avert a worldwide recession and financial and economic crisis. As a result, all efforts are now focused on this issue, while discussion of the original reasons for the war has receded.
Finally, mediation efforts must intensify, with other influential powers such as Europe and China joining the commendable efforts already being made by Pakistan, Oman and Qatar. Their involvement could give mediation greater weight, perhaps influencing the parties to the conflict and bringing them towards a compromise that safeguards everyone’s interests, ensures the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, spares the world a financial and economic crisis, and protects Arab states from bombardment and violations of their security and national sovereignty, even though they are not parties to this war.
The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

Ash-covered shoes and a president in crisis: A Reuters reporter remembers 9/11
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:07:39 UTC
19:07:39 KST

Ash-covered shoes and a president in crisis: A Reuters reporter remembers 9/11
WASHINGTON, Sept 9 - President George W. Bush was jogging around a Florida golf course before dawn when I first saw him on September 11, 2001.
As one of two Reuters correspondents traveling with Bush that day, I was covering what was expected to be a routine event with schoolchildren to promote his education policies. He had been president of the United States less than eight months.
Within hours, the untested Bush was confronting the worst attack on American soil since Pearl Harbor in 1941.
The tragedy unfolded as Bush visited the Emma E. Booker Elementary School in Sarasota, Florida. As the president was meeting staff and students, I was in a nearby press center set up for reporters. We watched a live television broadcast showing smoke pouring from one of the World Trade Center twin towers in New York. It had been hit by a plane in what we initially assumed was an accident. Then, as we watched, a second plane struck.
Bush was at the school, reading to children. Cameras captured the shocked look on his face as a White House aide entered the classroom and whispered to him about the second plane, saying "America is under attack."
By the end of the week, Bush would show a range of emotions as he came to grips with events that marked a turning point in his presidency and in American life — horror and anger at the attacks, grief and tears for the victims, and defiant promises to make those responsible pay.
The former president, now 80, plans to attend a ceremony on Friday to mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks at Ground Zero in New York. On Wednesday evening, he will share his reflections on the anniversary at his presidential library in Dallas, while 16 artworks he has painted reflecting the courage and sacrifice of that day will be on display.
"It became evident ... that the world had changed," Bush would later tell CBS's "60 Minutes II."
Bush spent the rest of his presidency working to prevent another such attack. The hijackings exposed security vulnerabilities, spurring increased safety measures at airports and public buildings. His administration drew fire for the harsh interrogation tactics used on some Islamic militant suspects, and his 2003 invasion of Iraq was seen by many as a costly mistake.
The former president declined an interview request from Reuters for this story.
SCRAMBLING TO PROTECT THE PRESIDENT
A quarter century later, the memories remain vivid.
In the immediate aftermath of the hijacked plane attacks, there was a scramble to protect the president. As Bush was whisked away to Air Force One to leave Florida, the scale of the crisis was becoming clear.
The World Trade Center towers collapsed, leading to the deaths of about 3,000 people. A third plane plowed into the Pentagon, killing 64 people on the plane and 125 in the building. A fourth plane slammed into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back against the hijackers, and all 44 people on board died.
Panic gripped Washington. Plumes of smoke from the Pentagon prompted fears of car bombs. The White House was evacuated, with the Secret Service telling female staffers to take off their heels and run.
Bush spent the day flying across the country on Air Force One, first to Barksdale Air Force Base in Louisiana and then to Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Later, he was to push for improved communications equipment on Air Force One after he had trouble staying in touch with the White House as he flew around the country.
In Nebraska, he entered an underground bunker to hold a teleconference briefing with top national security aides and Vice President Dick Cheney.
Eager to return to Washington, Bush arrived back at the White House late that afternoon. That night he gave an Oval Office address.
"The pictures of airplanes flying into buildings, fires burning, huge structures collapsing, have filled us with disbelief, terrible sadness, and a quiet, unyielding anger," Bush said.
Meanwhile, along with much of the White House press corps, I was still stranded in Florida, unable to fly anywhere as all air travel had been shut down. As president of the White House Correspondents' Association at the time, I helped push for our return home, and we finally took a chartered bus back to the capital.
After a 14-hour drive, our first view of Washington was the smoking gash in the Pentagon.
On September 14, I traveled with Bush to Ground Zero. The towers were still burning, the smell evident miles away. As Bush walked around the ravaged site with then-Mayor Rudy Giuliani, there were worries that some surrounding buildings had weakened to the point of collapse.
A thick layer of ash lay everywhere, on sidewalks, streets and on the shoulders of weary firefighters.
Standing on the remains of a firetruck, Bush told emergency crews that the United States was now at war with Islamic militants.
"I can hear you! I can hear you! The rest of the world hears you! And the people who knocked these buildings down will hear all of us soon!" he said through a bullhorn.
The shoes I wore that day were covered with ash and soot. When I got back home, I put them in a plastic bag and stowed them in a closet.
Twenty-five years later, there they remain. Too ruined to wear, too dear to throw away. REUTERS

How France fell in love with Céline Dion
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:07:24 UTC
19:07:24 KST

How France fell in love with Céline Dion
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Issued on:
Two years after her dazzling performance atop the Eiffel Tower for the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, Céline Dion is back in the French capital for a series of sold-out concerts – and fans are over the moon. Some 500,000 people are expected to attend the concerts.
In the Paris suburb of Nanterre, dozens of fans took part in a karaoke event organised by the city, hoping to win the last remaining tickets. “It takes me right back to my childhood,” said one fan who has been listening to the singer for four decades. For another fan, the Canadian singer is the true Queen of Pop: “I’d rather go and see Céline than Beyoncé or Lady Gaga. I love them too, but Céline is on another level!”
Another of her biggest admirers has made a career out of being Céline. Sébastien Costic has imitated Dion across Europe for the past 30 years. A former primary school teacher, when he performs, he has the full Céline look: custom-made accessories, gowns, wigs and high heels. Since the announcement of Céline’s comeback, bookings for his tribute shows have doubled.
For Costic, Dion holds a very special place in the hearts of French people: “Today, you almost forget that she isn’t French. You feel like she’s one of us (...) because she’s so close to people – in her attitude, her popularity, and through the songs she’s shared with the world. She has also helped people around the world discover the French language.”
After being diagnosed with a rare and debilitating neurological condition, Dion was forced to put her career on hold in early 2020. Then, against all odds, she made a surprise appearance on the Eiffel Tower during the Paris Olympic Games. Her resilience was celebrated around the world.
“D’eux”: A turning point
In 1994, Céline Dion teamed up with popular French song-writer Jean-Jacques Goldman for the album D’eux. Their partnership struck the right chord: around 11 million copies were sold, making it the best-selling French-language album of all time. Co-producer Erick Benzi explains in this edition of France in Focus that, “In the United States, a singer’s voice is often used as an instrument. In France, we’re more into storytelling”.
Dion rethought the way she sang. It took her “roughly ten seconds” to understand that in French, she didn’t need to push every single note, Benzi recalls. As a result, Céline recorded three songs in one day, instead of one. Her extraordinary efficiency earned her the nickname OVNI or “Objet Vocal Non Identifié (Unidentified Vocal Object, a play on words of the acronym OVNI which stands for Objet Volant Non Identifié – the equivalent of UFO in English).
A star who keeps it real
Céline Dion’s voice is not the only reason for her vast success. She has won audiences over with her generosity and her genuine connection with fans. “She’s incredibly sincere. She doesn’t act like she’s a star”, says Thérèse Zaydman, adding “Céline Dion is the youngest of 14 children. Her parents didn’t have much money. When she was little, she slept in the drawer of a dresser! So I think she’s stayed true to her roots.”
Céline has never shied away from sharing the challenges she has faced in life: the death of her husband, René Angélil, her personal struggles and, in 2022, her diagnosis with stiff-person syndrome.
Two years later, her surprise appearance on the Eiffel Tower, where she performed “L’Hymne à l’amour”, moved the entire nation. Today, fans are counting down the days until they can finally see their idol on stage: the international superstar who calls France her second "chez moi”.

Aktif Bank becomes first Turkish bank to join China's global yuan payment system
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:06:28 UTC
19:06:28 KST

Aktif Bank has become the first Turkish bank to join China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), marking a step towards expanding financial ties between Türkiye and China.
The agreement was signed on the sidelines of the China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT). CIPS facilitates international payments and settlements in Chinese yuan, potentially reducing the time and costs associated with traditional multi-currency conversions.
The bank plans to make CIPS payments available through its digital banking platform, allowing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as well as larger companies to conduct yuan-denominated transactions more efficiently.
Growing yuan use creates new opportunities
Aktif Bank General Manager Aysegul Adaca Ogan said CIPS, developed by the People’s Bank of China, has expanded significantly over the past five years and now serves more than 1,800 participating banks.
She said yuan-denominated payments accounted for 28 percent of China’s foreign trade volume, worth around $6 trillion, over the past five years, while trade between Türkiye and China doubled from $25 billion to $50 billion over the same period.
“With rising yuan payments in Chinese foreign trade and the growing demand for yuan payment systems in Türkiye, joining this platform has been a viable opportunity for us,” Ogan said.
Aktif Bank targets wider global payment corridors
Ogan said the bank aims to expand its international payment network beyond Europe and the Americas, with China becoming an important part of its long-term strategy.
“We have over 1,300 banks worldwide, and we want to expand our corridor to include regions like China after Europe and the Americas, after closely monitoring opportunities in the Chinese market,” she said.
Ogan added that Aktif Bank’s participation in CIFIT as the only Turkish bank represented an important step in strengthening its presence in the Chinese market.

Chinese authorities have officially confirmed that all 33 missing Latvian nationals had been in China and have no information indicating that the travellers crossed the border back into Nepal, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) told LETA.
According to the MFA, this means that the Latvian nationals were most likely on the Tibetan side of the Himalayas when the catastrophic floods and mudslides struck. Chinese authorities have also asked Latvia to provide DNA samples for comparison.
It was previously reported that belongings belonging to the travellers had been found on the Chinese side near the border crossing. The MFA is currently determining whether the items will be photographed and whether the images will be made available for identification. Meanwhile, Red Cross DNA experts are expected to arrive in Nepal this week to speed up and facilitate the comparison of samples.
MFA Consular Department representative Jurģis Barkāns, who is currently in Nepal, is also exploring options for transporting to Latvia the travellers’ belongings left behind at hotels.
The MFA noted that the amount of belongings must first be established
and it must be determined whether the items can be identified. Arrangements could then be made with transport companies to bring them to Latvia.
The MFA stressed that not all relatives have received or fully understood the information sent last week regarding the necessary steps and formalities. Relatives have been sent a detailed explanation compiling information from the Ministry of Welfare, Ministry of Justice, Latvian Association of Local and Regional Governments, and Ministry of Education and Science. On Wednesday, the Ministry of Justice will hold a meeting with relatives to explain the information provided and answer their questions.
The MFA is also asking relatives who are not currently on the ministry’s contact list but believe they should receive information directly to get in touch. The ministry stressed that it is currently important for all relatives to obtain a certificate confirming the travellers’ status as missing persons. The Latvian nationals have been placed on an international missing persons list, and relatives need the relevant certificate to complete other formalities.
The Chancery of the President of Latvia has also asked the MFA to contact the Ombudsman, who is prepared, where possible, to advise both the ministry and the relatives of the missing people.
Information about this option has been sent to the relatives.
As previously reported, the collapse of a glacier on the 26th of August triggered a flow of ice debris, causing water and mud to surge from a glacial lake and resulting in widespread destruction in Nepal and China. As of the 3rd of September, the confirmed death toll had reached 1,252, while another 4,216 people were considered missing.
A large group of Latvian tourists organised by yoga enthusiasts from Yantra was also near the epicentre of the disaster, while a smaller number of Latvian tourists were in the disaster zone as part of a group organised by the local company Mighty Himalayan Trek. The MFA is aware that three Latvian residents who were in the region at the time were not affected by the flood-triggered mudslide in Nepal, while 33 are currently considered missing.

The 23-year-old man who was arrested at the Brussels South railway station with a loaded Kalashnikov last week says that he came into possession of the military grade weapon by chance and had come to Belgium to sell it. The man appeared before the Brussels magistrates’ court today.
Suspect found with Kalashnikov at Brussels South says he stole the weapon ‘by chance’
“My client came into possession of the weapon in the Lille area of France,” his lawyer Benoit Lemal told the court. “Whilst moving house, he saw a car left unlocked and unattended. He took the opportunity to steal a bag from the vehicle. To his great surprise, he found a weapon inside the bag.”

No plea for release

A second suspect, also in his twenties, appeared before the court this morning too. “According to the public prosecutor’s office, my client is a member of a criminal organisation involved in arms trafficking, but he denies this,” his lawyer Mustapha El Hajjami says. He asked the court to place his client under electronic monitoring.
In the event the court decided that both suspects would remain in gaol.

Over 20,000 olim made Aliyah to Israel from 100 countries in past year, data shows
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:03:30 UTC
19:03:30 KST

More than 20,000 new immigrants arrived in Israel during the Jewish year 5786 (September 23, 2025 to September 3, 2026), coming from over 100 different countries worldwide, according to a new data report released by the Aliyah and Integration Ministry and the Jewish Agency.
The breakdown of the Aliyah figures released on Tuesday for the past year shows that Russia topped the charts with 5,685 olim (immigrants to Israel) arriving in Israel, followed by 4,364 from France, 3,333 from the United States, and 975 from the United Kingdom.
Additionally, 797 olim came from Ukraine, 491 from Belarus, 440 from Canada, 247 from Australia, 243 from Argentina, 241 from Georgia, 210 from South Africa, 210 from Germany, and 200 from Brazil.
Olim of all age groups
The data also showed that 35% of the olim were people aged 18-35, reflecting significant growth in Israeli society and the economy.
According to the data report, many of these young immigrants were physicians and professionals in in-demand fields. Some 24% of the olim are children and youth up to age 17, who have now been integrated into the Israeli education system. An additional 18% are aged 36-50, 9% are aged 51-60, 5% are aged 61-65, and 10% are 66 or older.
The two oldest olim this year were both 102 years old at the time of their arrival in the country – one from Russia and one from France. The youngest was a two-week-old infant who arrived with his family from Mexico.
Where are Olim making their start?
About 31% of all olim this year settled in communities north of Hadera or south of Ashdod. Specifically, 3,862 olim (about 20% of the total) settled from Hadera northward, while 2,247 (about 11%) settled from Ashdod southward.
Tel Aviv attracted the largest number of new olim this year, with 2,762 newcomers, followed by Netanya (2,224), Jerusalem (2,134), Haifa (1,504), Ra’anana (1,042), Bat Yam (957), Ashdod (846), Beit Shemesh (680), Ashkelon (534), and Rishon LeZion (450). Nahariya, the northernmost city on the list, absorbed 307 olim, while Eilat, the southernmost, welcomed 132.
'The essence of Zionism'
Reflecting the year’s data, the Aliyah and Integration Ministry and the Jewish Agency touched on the Diasporas connection to the Jewish state, stating in the report, “Even in a year marked by a challenging security situation, thousands of Jews from every corner of the globe chose to make aliyah to Israel, build their homes there, and raise their children there – a choice that reflects the deep and enduring connection between world Jewry and the State of Israel.”
Maj.-Gen. (res.) Doron Almog, chairman of the Jewish Agency, commented on the Aliyah numbers during a challenging year, stating that they represent “the essence of Zionism.”
“Aliyah is the strongest response to every challenge we face; it serves as a growth engine that contributes to strengthening the State of Israel,” Almog said.
Aliyah and Integration Minister Ofir Sofer emphasized, “Every oleh who arrives strengthens society, the economy, and the resilience of the country, and aliyah is a central component of its future.”

Israeli student grades dropping sharply, initial national evaluation report confirms
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-09
10:03:29 UTC
19:03:29 KST

Israeli students have seen a major drop in grades and performance, according to an initial, not yet formally verified, report by the National Authority for Measurement and Evaluation in Education (known by its Hebrew acronym, RAMA), confirmed on Tuesday.
Education Minister Yoav Kisch released the RAMA report after the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) published the international Program for International Student Assessment (PISA) results on Tuesday, with officials describing the findings as a "catastrophic event on a historic scale."
According to RAMA's initial findings, which the Education Ministry emphasized were not final, only 3% of 9th-grade students were considered to be fully fulfilling the ministry's requirements in their science and technology education programs, with another 16% considered "near" full requirement fulfillment.
The number of students fully fulfilling the Education Ministry's requirements was higher in 6th-grade English (36%), mathematics (37%), and Hebrew (20%).
These results were consistent with the PISA results, in which, compared with the previous PISA tests in 2022, Israeli students fell eight places in science, seven in reading, and six in mathematics.
Across all three subjects, Israel's 2025 PISA results were the lowest ever recorded for the country.
Kisch attempts to delay RAMA release showcasing tenure failures
Every three years, RAMA and the Education Ministry publish a detailed national analysis simultaneously with, or close to, the OECD's official publication.
But long after the organization had granted media representatives full access to the data, and despite the publication being known about and scheduled years in advance, Kisch's representatives and officials from the measurement authority still had not managed to "complete the necessary coordination regarding the format of publication."
In other words, while Kisch could not prevent the publication of the embarrassing report, which presents his tenure as a failure, he tried to delay it until the last moment and held a media "briefing" at the exact time the report was released.
According to KAN News, several weeks ago Kisch requested that the RAMA report not be published on the same day as the PISA results.
Kisch published the results that day regardless, KAN reported, after the government's legal advisor said he did not have the authority to withhold the findings and after RAMA told him it intended to publish the results that day.
KAN also cited the Education Ministry as saying that the RAMA findings "are under external professional review in light of the claims raised by the ministry."
Yuval Bagno contributed to this report.
